title.zh: 卷一百八十二 列傳第七十 王恕 馬文升 劉大夏
title.en: Volume 182 Biographies 70: Wang Shu, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia
title.raw: 卷一百八十二 列傳第七十 王恕 馬文升 劉大夏 Volume 182 Biographies 70: Wang Shu, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia

sentences.zh: 王恕，字宗貫，三原人。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, styled Zongguan, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, whose courtesy name was Zongguan, came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授大理左評事，進左寺副。

translations.literal: From his post as a Hanlin bachelor he was appointed Left Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to Vice Director of the Left Tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a Hanlin bachelor, he was made Left Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review and later promoted to Vice Director of the Left Tribunal.

sentences.zh: 嘗條刑罰不中者六事，皆議行之。

translations.literal: He once set forth six matters in which punishments were improper; all were debated and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He once listed six abuses in the penal code, and every one was adopted after deliberation.

sentences.zh: 遷揚州知府，發粟振饑不待報，作資政書院以課士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Yangzhou, issued grain to relieve famine without awaiting approval, and founded the Zizheng Academy to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Yangzhou he opened the granaries to feed the hungry without waiting for imperial leave, and established the Zizheng Academy to train local students.

sentences.zh: 天順四年以治行最，超遷江西右布政使，平贛州寇。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun, for the finest record of governance he was promoted over the usual steps to Right Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi and pacified the bandits of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun his outstanding administration won him a leap promotion to Right Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, where he put down the rebels in Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，詔大臣嚴核天下方面官，乃黜河南左布政使侯臣等十三人，而以恕代臣。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor succeeded, the court ordered senior ministers to scrutinize frontier officials strictly; thirteen men including Hou Chen, Left Administration Commissioner of Henan, were dismissed, and Shu replaced Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On Xianzong's accession the throne ordered a rigorous review of regional officials throughout the empire; thirteen were removed, among them Hou Chen, Left Administration Commissioner of Henan, and Shu was appointed in Chen's place.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，南陽、荊、襄流民嘯聚為亂，擢恕右副都御史撫治之。會丁母憂，詔奔喪兩月即起視事。恕辭，不許。與尚書白圭共平大盜劉通，復討破其黨石龍。嚴束所部毋濫殺，流民復業。移撫河南。論功，進左副都御史，稍遷南京刑部右侍郎。父憂，服除，以原官總督河道。浚高郵、邵伯諸湖，修雷公、上下句城、陳公四塘水閘。因災變，請講求弭災策。帝為賜山東租一年，畿輔亦多減免。旋改南京戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, displaced people in Nanyang, Jing, and Xiang gathered in shouting bands and rose in disorder, and Shu was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to pacify and govern them. Just then he encountered mourning for his mother; an edict ordered him to hasten to the funeral and, after two months, resume his duties. Shu declined, but permission was not granted. Together with Minister Bai Gui he pacified the great bandit Liu Tong, and again attacked and defeated Liu Tong's follower Shi Long. He strictly restrained his subordinates so that they would not kill indiscriminately, and the displaced people returned to their occupations. He was transferred to govern Henan. In recognition of merit, he was advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and somewhat later transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing. When his father died, and after the mourning period ended, he was made overseer of the river works with his former office. He dredged the lakes at Gaoyou and Shaobo, and repaired the sluices at the four ponds of Leigong, Upper and Lower Jucheng, and Chengong. Because of disasters and anomalies, he requested that policies for averting disasters be examined. The emperor therefore remitted one year of taxes in Shandong, and many taxes in the capital region were also reduced or remitted. Soon afterward he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua, displaced people in Nanyang, Jing, and Xiang gathered into rebellious bands, and Shu was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to pacify the region. When his mother died, an edict allowed him to attend the funeral but ordered him back to duty after two months. Shu declined, but the court refused. Together with Minister Bai Gui he defeated the major rebel Liu Tong, then defeated Liu Tong's follower Shi Long as well. He kept his forces under strict discipline, forbidding indiscriminate killing, and the refugees returned to their livelihoods. Transferred to govern Henan, he was promoted for his merit to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and later became Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing. After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he resumed office as overseer of river works. He dredged the Gaoyou and Shaobo lakes and repaired the sluices at the four ponds of Leigong, Upper and Lower Jucheng, and Chengong. In response to disasters and portents, he asked the court to study measures to avert calamity. The emperor accordingly remitted a year of taxes in Shandong, and also reduced or remitted many levies in the capital region. Shu was soon transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大學士商輅等以雲南遠在萬里，西控諸夷，南接交阯，而鎮守中官錢能貪恣甚，議遣大臣有威望者為巡撫鎮壓之，乃改恕左副都御史以行，就進右都御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Grand Secretaries including Shang Lu, because Yunnan lay ten thousand li away, controlled the western tribes and bordered Jiaozhi, while the eunuch defender Qian Neng was extremely greedy and overbearing, proposed sending a senior minister of standing as grand coordinator to suppress him; Shu was therefore changed to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief for the mission and promoted on departure to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Grand Secretaries, led by Shang Lu, argued that Yunnan—remote, flanked by barbarians on the west and Jiaozhi on the south—needed a minister of weight to rein in the rapacious eunuch defender Qian Neng; Shu was accordingly reassigned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief with immediate promotion to Right Censor-in-Chief for the journey.

sentences.zh: 初，能遣指揮郭景奏事京師，言安南捕盜兵闌入雲南境，帝即命景賫敕戒約之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Neng had sent the commander Guo Jing to report at the capital that Annamese troops pursuing bandits had strayed into Yunnan; the emperor at once ordered Jing to carry an edict of warning and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Neng had dispatched Commander Guo Jing to the capital with word that Annamese soldiers hunting robbers had crossed into Yunnan; the emperor promptly sent Jing back with an edict of admonition.

sentences.zh: 舊制，使安南必由廣西，而景直自雲南往。

translations.literal: By established practice envoys to Annam had to go through Guangxi, but Jing went straight from Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations envoys to Annam had to travel via Guangxi, yet Jing took the route directly from Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 能因景遺安南王黎灝玉帶、寶絳、蟒衣、珍奇諸物。

translations.literal: Neng used Jing to send the Annamese king Le Hao a jade belt, jeweled sash, python robe, and other rare objects.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jing, Neng presented King Le Hao of Annam with a jade belt, jeweled sash, python robe, and other curiosities.

sentences.zh: 灝遣將率兵送景還，欲遂通雲南道。

translations.literal: Hao sent a general with troops to escort Jing back, intending to open a route through Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao dispatched a general with soldiers to escort Jing home, hoping thereby to establish a passage through Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 景懼後禍，紿先行白守關者。

translations.literal: Jing, fearing future punishment, deceived them by going ahead to inform the border guards.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid of later retribution, Jing tricked them by riding ahead to warn the frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 因脫歸，揚言安南寇至，關吏戒嚴。

translations.literal: He then slipped back and spread word that Annamese raiders were coming; the gate officers went on full alert.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped back first, crying that Annamese invaders were at hand, and the pass officials raised the alarm.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐琮遣人諭其帥，始返。

translations.literal: The Duke of Qian, Mu Cong, sent men to instruct their commander, and they only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Cong, Duke of Qian, sent envoys to admonish their commander, and the troops at last turned back.

sentences.zh: 而諸臣畏能，匿不奏。

translations.literal: Yet the officials, fearing Neng, concealed the affair and did not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: The local officials, terrified of Neng, kept silent and never reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 能又頻遣景及指揮盧安、蘇本等交通幹崖、孟密諸土官，納其金寶無算。

translations.literal: Neng also repeatedly sent Jing and the commanders Lu An and Su Ben to deal with the native chiefs of Ganyao, Mengmi, and others, taking untold gold and jewels from them.
translations.idiomatic: Neng likewise kept dispatching Jing, Lu An, Su Ben, and other commanders to traffic with the native offices of Ganyao and Mengmi, extorting countless treasures.

sentences.zh: 恕皆廉得之。

translations.literal: Shu investigated and learned of it all.
translations.idiomatic: Shu uncovered every detail through his inquiries.

sentences.zh: 遣騎執景，景懼自殺，因劾能私通外國，罪當死。

translations.literal: He sent riders to seize Jing; Jing, in fear, killed himself; Shu then impeached Neng for private dealings with foreign states, a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: He sent horsemen to arrest Jing, who committed suicide in terror; Shu then charged Neng with clandestine relations abroad, punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 詔遣刑部郎中潘蕃往按之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Pan Fan of the Ministry of Justice to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Pan Fan, a director in the Ministry of Justice, to conduct an on-site inquiry.

sentences.zh: 能又以其間，驛進黃鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the interval Neng hurried a courier tribute of yellow parrots to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Neng rushed a relay gift of yellow parrots to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 恕請禁絕，且盡發能貪暴狀，言：「昔交阯以鎮守非人，致一方陷沒。

translations.literal: Shu petitioned to ban the tribute and laid bare all of Neng's rapacity, saying: "Once before Jiaozhi was ruined because the wrong man held the frontier command, and an entire province was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shu petitioned to halt the tribute and exposed the full extent of Neng's greed and violence, writing: "Jiaozhi was lost before because the wrong man was put in charge of the frontier, until a whole region fell.

sentences.zh: 今日之事殆又甚焉。

translations.literal: Today's affair is perhaps even worse.
translations.idiomatic: What we face today may be worse still.

sentences.zh: 陛下何惜一能，不以安邊僥。」

translations.literal: Why should Your Majesty spare one Neng and not secure the borderlands?"
translations.idiomatic: Why keep a single Neng when the safety of the frontier is at stake?"

sentences.zh: 能大懼，急屬貴近請召恕還。

translations.literal: Neng was greatly alarmed and urgently asked his patrons at court to have Shu recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Neng was terrified and at once prevailed on his court allies to summon Shu back.

sentences.zh: 而是時商輅、項忠諸正人方以忤汪直罷，遂改恕掌南京都察院，參贊守備機務。

translations.literal: At that time upright men such as Shang Lu and Xiang Zhong had just been dismissed for opposing Wang Zhi, so Shu was reassigned to head the Nanjing Censorate and to assist in frontier defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Shang Lu, Xiang Zhong, and other honest ministers had been ousted for crossing Wang Zhi; Shu was shifted to direct the Nanjing Censorate and advise on garrison matters.

sentences.zh: 能事立解，藩勘上得實，置不問。

translations.literal: Neng's case was quickly closed; Pan's investigation found the facts true, yet nothing was done.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's trouble dissolved at once: Pan's report confirmed the charges, but no punishment followed.

sentences.zh: 恕居雲南九月，威行僥外，黔國以下鹹惕息奉令。

translations.literal: Shu spent nine months in Yunnan; his authority reached beyond the frontier, and from the Duke of Qian downward all stood in awe and obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: During nine months in Yunnan his prestige extended past the borderlands; from the Duke of Qian on down everyone submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 疏凡二十上，直聲動天下。

translations.literal: He submitted twenty memorials in all, and his forthright voice shook the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He filed twenty memorials in all, and the force of his honest remonstrance resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 當是時，安南納江西叛人王姓者為謀主，潛遣諜入臨安，又於蒙自市銅鑄兵器，將伺間襲雲南。

translations.literal: At that time Annam had taken a Jiangxi rebel surnamed Wang as strategist, secretly sent spies into Lin'an, and at Mengzi was buying copper to cast weapons, intending to strike Yunnan when chance offered.
translations.idiomatic: Annam had meanwhile sheltered a Jiangxi rebel named Wang as mastermind, slipped agents into Lin'an, and at Mengzi purchased copper to forge arms, plotting to raid Yunnan at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 恕請增設副使二員，以飭邊備，謀遂沮。

translations.literal: Shu asked that two additional vice commissioners be appointed to tighten frontier defense, and the plot was thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu requested two extra vice commissioners to stiffen border defenses, and the conspiracy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 還南京數月，遷兵部尚書，參贊如故。

translations.literal: After several months back in Nanjing he was moved to Minister of War, retaining his advisory duties.
translations.idiomatic: A few months after returning to Nanjing he was appointed Minister of War while keeping his advisory role.

sentences.zh: 考選官屬，嚴拒請托，同事者鹹不悅。

translations.literal: In selecting subordinates he sternly refused patronage; his colleagues were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted official selections and flatly rejected favor-seeking; his fellow ministers resented it.

sentences.zh: 而錢能歸，屢譖恕於帝。

translations.literal: When Qian Neng returned he repeatedly slandered Shu to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian Neng came back to court he repeatedly maligned Shu before the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝亦銜恕數直言，遂命兼右副都御史巡撫南畿。

translations.literal: The emperor also resented Shu's frequent blunt speech and therefore ordered him additionally to serve as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief grand coordinator of the Southern Metropolitan Region.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already annoyed by Shu's bluntness, ordered him to take on the additional post of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of the southern capital districts.

sentences.zh: 舊制，應天、鎮江、太平、寧國、廣德官田征半租，民田全免。

translations.literal: Under the old system, official fields in Yingtian, Zhenjiang, Taiping, Ningguo, and Guangde paid half rent while private fields were wholly exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in Yingtian, Zhenjiang, Taiping, Ningguo, and Guangde, government land paid half the grain tax and private land none at all.

sentences.zh: 其後，民田率歸豪右，而官田累貧民。

translations.literal: Later private fields mostly passed to great families while official fields were piled on poor households.
translations.idiomatic: In time private holdings passed chiefly to powerful landlords, and official plots were shifted onto the poor.

sentences.zh: 恕乃量減官田耗，稍增之民田。

translations.literal: Shu therefore reduced the surcharge on official fields and slightly increased that on private fields.
translations.idiomatic: Shu cut the extra levies on official land and raised those on private land a little.

sentences.zh: 常州時有羨米，乃奏以六萬石補夏稅，又補他府戶口鹽鈔六百萬貫，公私便焉。

translations.literal: Changzhou then had surplus grain; he memorialized that sixty thousand shi be used to offset the summer tax, and also made up six million strings of household salt certificates for other prefectures—public and private interests alike were eased.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhou held surplus grain he proposed applying sixty thousand shi to the summer levy and covering six million strings of salt certificates owed by other prefectures, to everyone's relief.

sentences.zh: 所部水災，奏免秋糧六十余萬石。

translations.literal: Where his jurisdiction suffered flood, he memorialized to remit more than six hundred thousand shi of autumn grain.
translations.idiomatic: After floods in his region he secured remission of over six hundred thousand shi of autumn grain tax.

sentences.zh: 周行振貸，全活二百余萬口。

translations.literal: He toured distributing relief and saved more than two million lives.
translations.idiomatic: Touring the stricken areas with relief grain, he kept more than two million people alive.

sentences.zh: 江南歲輸白糧，民多至破產，而光祿概以給庖人、賤工。

translations.literal: The south yearly delivered white rice, often driving commoners to ruin, while the Court of Imperial Entertainments used it indiscriminately for cooks and menial workers.
translations.idiomatic: Southern taxpayers shipped white rice until many families were ruined, yet the Court of Imperial Entertainments fed it to kitchen staff and low artisans.

sentences.zh: 又中官暴橫，四方輸上供物，監收者率要羨入。

translations.literal: Eunuchs too were violent and overbearing; wherever tribute was delivered the supervising eunuchs usually demanded surplus as their cut.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs bullied the regions as well: those who supervised tribute collections routinely extorted extra shares.

sentences.zh: 織造繒采及采花卉禽鳥者，絡繹道路。

translations.literal: Weavers of silks and brocades and collectors of flowers, birds, and curios filled the roads in endless files.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys weaving silks and brocades and gathering flowers, birds, and exotic goods clogged the highways.

sentences.zh: 恕先後論列，皆不納。

translations.literal: Shu repeatedly argued these points, but none was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu protested again and again, yet every plea was ignored.

sentences.zh: 中官王敬挾妖人千戶王臣南行采藥物、珍玩，所至騷然，長吏多被辱。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Jing, taking the sorcerer Wang Chen, a chiliarch, south to gather drugs and treasures, disturbed every place they passed and many local heads were humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Jing traveled south with the magician Wang Chen, a chiliarch, to collect drugs and curios; wherever they went they caused uproar and many magistrates were insulted.

sentences.zh: 至蘇州，召諸生寫妖書，諸生大嘩。

translations.literal: At Suzhou he summoned students to copy sorcerous books, and the students raised a great outcry.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Suzhou he ordered students to transcribe occult texts, and they erupted in protest.

sentences.zh: 敬奏諸生抗命。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized that the students had defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reported that the students had disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 恕亟疏言：「當此兇歲，宜遣使振濟，顧乃橫索玩好。

translations.literal: Shu immediately memorialized, saying: "In this disastrous year, an envoy should be sent to provide relief; instead, they are extorting curiosities.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote at once: "In a famine year the court should dispatch relief, yet these men brazenly demand playthings.

sentences.zh: 昔唐太宗諷梁州獻名鷹，明皇令益州織半臂褙子，進琵琶桿撥鏤牙合子諸物，李大亮、蘇颋不奉詔。

translations.literal: Of old, when Liangzhou offered Emperor Taizong of Tang a famous hawk, and Emperor Ming of Tang ordered Yizhou to weave half-sleeve jackets and sent inlaid ivory cases for pipa pegs and the like, Li Daliang and Su Ting refused the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Li Daliang and Su Ting refused imperial orders when Liangzhou presented a famous hawk to Tang Taizong and when Tang Minghuang demanded half-sleeve jackets from Yizhou and inlaid ivory fittings for pipa pegs.

sentences.zh: 臣雖無似，有慕斯人。」

translations.literal: Though I am far beneath those men, I aspire to follow them."
translations.idiomatic: I am no match for those worthies, yet I wish to emulate them."

sentences.zh: 因盡列敬等罪狀。

translations.literal: He therefore listed all the crimes of Jing and his party.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to enumerate every offense of Jing and his followers.

sentences.zh: 敬亦誣奏恕並及常州知府孫仁，仁被逮。

translations.literal: Jing also falsely accused Shu and implicated Sun Ren, prefect of Changzhou, who was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Jing struck back with false charges against Shu and dragged in Sun Ren, prefect of Changzhou, who was seized.

sentences.zh: 仁，新淦人，由進士歷知府，為人方峻，敬至不為禮，以是見忤。

translations.literal: Ren, a native of Xin'gan, had risen through the jinshi to prefect; he was upright and stern, and when Jing arrived offered no courtesy—hence the grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ren of Xin'gan, a jinshi who had served as prefect, was a man of severe integrity; he refused to defer to Jing, and for that was targeted.

sentences.zh: 恕抗章救，三疏劾敬。

translations.literal: Shu submitted urgent memorials in his defense and three times impeached Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fought the case with bold memorials and thrice impeached Jing.

sentences.zh: 會中官尚銘亦發敬奸狀，乃下敬等獄，戍其黨十九人，而棄臣市，傳首南京。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the eunuch Shang Ming also exposed Jing's villainy; Jing and his fellows were imprisoned, nineteen partisans were banished, and Chen was executed in the market with his head displayed at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Shang Ming exposed Jing's crimes, Jing was thrown into prison, nineteen accomplices were exiled, and Chen was beheaded in the marketplace with his head hung at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 仁亦得釋歸，後積官至巡撫寧夏右副都御史。

translations.literal: Ren was released and later rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ren was freed and eventually became Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 二十年復改恕南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Shu was again made Nanjing Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Shu was once more appointed Nanjing Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時錢能亦守備南京，語人曰：「王公，天人也，吾敬事而已。」

translations.literal: At that time Qian Neng was also garrisoning Nanjing and told others, "Lord Wang is a man of heaven; I can only serve him with respect."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng, then defending Nanjing, said to acquaintances, "Lord Wang is a heaven-sent man; all I can do is honor him."

sentences.zh: 恕坦懷待之，能卒斂戢。

translations.literal: Shu treated him openly and without suspicion, and Neng in the end restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shu met him with frank goodwill, and Neng finally curbed his conduct.

sentences.zh: 林俊之下獄也，恕言：「天地止一壇，祖宗止一廟，而佛至千余寺。

translations.literal: When Lin Jun was imprisoned, Shu argued: "Heaven and earth have only one altar, and the ancestors only one temple, yet Buddhist temples number more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Jun was imprisoned, Shu argued: "Heaven and earth have a single altar and the ancestors a single temple, yet Buddhist temples exceed a thousand.

sentences.zh: 一寺立，而移民居且數百家，費內帑且數十萬，此舛也。

translations.literal: Each temple established displaces hundreds of households and costs the privy purse hundreds of thousands—this is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Every new monastery moves hundreds of families and drains the treasury by hundreds of thousands—such waste is wrong.

sentences.zh: 俊言當，不宜罪。」

translations.literal: Jun spoke correctly and should not be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun was right and ought not to suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 帝得疏不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor, receiving the memorial, was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with displeasure.

sentences.zh: 恕侃侃論列無少避。

translations.literal: Yet Shu argued forthrightly without the least evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Still Shu spoke plainly and shrank from nothing.

sentences.zh: 先後應詔陳言者二十一，建白者三十九，皆力阻權幸。

translations.literal: In all he answered twenty-one imperial summonses to speak and made thirty-nine constructive proposals, every one aimed at blocking the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He responded to twenty-one imperial calls for counsel and offered thirty-nine concrete reforms, each thwarting the favorites.

sentences.zh: 天下傾心慕之，遇朝事有不可，必曰：「王公胡不言也？」

translations.literal: The empire looked up to him; whenever court affairs went awry people would always say, "Why does Lord Wang not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: All China admired him; whenever policy went wrong, people would cry, "Why is Lord Wang silent?"

sentences.zh: 則又曰：「公疏且至矣」，已，恕疏果至。

translations.literal: Then they would add, 'His memorial will arrive soon'—and indeed Shu's paper would come.
translations.idiomatic: Others answered, 'His memorial is on its way'—and soon Shu's dispatch would appear.

sentences.zh: 時為謠曰：「兩京十二部，獨有一王恕。」

translations.literal: A popular rhyme ran: "Of the twelve ministries in the two capitals, Wang Shu stands alone."
translations.idiomatic: People sang: "Among the twelve ministries of both capitals, only Wang Shu remains upright."

sentences.zh: 於是貴近皆側目，帝亦頗厭苦之。

translations.literal: The powerful therefore glared at him, and the emperor too grew weary of him.
translations.idiomatic: The mighty resented him, and even the emperor wearied of his remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 二十二年起用傳奉官，恕諫尤切，帝愈不悅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when honorary court attendants were reappointed, Shu's remonstrance was especially sharp and the emperor grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the throne revived honorary palace posts; Shu's opposition was especially fierce and the emperor's irritation deepened.

sentences.zh: 恕先加太子少保，會南京兵部侍郎馬顯乞罷，忽附批落恕宮保致仕，朝野大駭。

translations.literal: Shu had earlier been made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; when Ma Xian, vice minister of war at Nanjing, begged to retire, a sudden marginal note stripped Shu of his guardian title and ordered retirement—the court and country were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had been named Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; when Ma Xian, Nanjing vice minister of war, asked to resign, a sudden marginal order removed Shu's guardian rank and sent him home—shock swept the realm.

sentences.zh: 恕數為巡撫，歷侍郎至尚書，皆在留都。

translations.literal: Shu had several times served as grand coordinator, rising from vice minister to minister, always at the southern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had repeatedly been grand coordinator and risen from vice minister to minister, always in the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 以好直言，終不得立朝。

translations.literal: Because he loved to speak plainly he never held office at the northern court.
translations.idiomatic: His outspokenness kept him from ever serving in the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 既歸，名益高，臺省推薦無虛月。

translations.literal: After retirement his fame only grew; censorial offices recommended him month after month without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement his reputation soared; the censorate and ministries recommended him endlessly.

sentences.zh: 工部主事仙居王純比恕汲黯，至予杖，謫思南推官。

translations.literal: Wang Chun of Xianju, a director in the Ministry of Works, compared Shu to Ji An; for this he was beaten with the rod and demoted to push-official of Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chun of Xianju, a Works director, likened Shu to Ji An; he was flogged and banished to Sinan as push-official.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，始用廷臣薦，召入為吏部尚書，尋加太子太保。先是，中外劾大學士劉吉者，必薦恕，吉以是大恚。凡恕所推舉，必陰撓之。弘治元年閏正月，言官劾兩廣總督宋旻、漕運總督邱鼐等三十七人宜降黜，中多素有時望者。吉竟取中旨允之，章不下吏部。恕以不得其職，拜疏乞去，不許。陜西缺巡撫，恕推河南布政使蕭禎。詔別推，恕執奏曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，任臣銓部。倘所舉不效，臣罪也。今陛下安知禎不才而拒之？是必左右近臣意有所屬。臣不能承望風指，以固祿位。且陛下既以禎為不可用，是臣不可用也，願乞骸骨。」帝乃卒用禎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, only then, on the recommendation of court ministers, was Shu summoned in as Minister of Personnel, and soon he was additionally made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Previously, whenever officials inside and outside the capital impeached Grand Secretary Liu Ji, they always recommended Shu, and for this Ji was greatly enraged. Whenever Shu recommended someone for appointment, Ji would secretly obstruct it. In the intercalary first month of the first year of Hongzhi, remonstrance officials impeached thirty-seven men, including Song Min, supreme commander of the two Guang, and Qiu Nai, supreme commander of grain transport, as deserving demotion or dismissal; among them were many who had long enjoyed contemporary prestige. Ji finally obtained an inner imperial command approving it, and the memorial was not sent down to the Ministry of Personnel. Shu, because he could not exercise his office, bowed and submitted a memorial begging to leave, but this was not permitted. When Shaanxi lacked a grand coordinator, Shu recommended Xiao Zhen, Administration Commissioner of Henan. An edict ordered him to make another recommendation, but Shu insisted in a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty did not consider your servant unworthy, and entrusted your servant with the Ministry of Personnel. If the person I recommend proves ineffective, the fault is mine. Now how does Your Majesty know that Zhen is untalented and reject him? This must be because attendants close to Your Majesty have their own preference. Your servant cannot look for the direction of the wind and submit to it in order to secure salary and position. Moreover, since Your Majesty considers Zhen unusable, this means your servant too is unusable; I beg to return my bones." The emperor finally used Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne, Shu was at last summoned on the recommendation of court ministers and made Minister of Personnel; soon afterward he was also appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Earlier, officials at court and in the provinces who impeached Grand Secretary Liu Ji always recommended Shu, which infuriated Ji. Whenever Shu put someone forward, Ji quietly blocked the appointment. In the intercalary first month of the first year of Hongzhi, remonstrance officials impeached thirty-seven men, including Song Min, supreme commander of the two Guang, and Qiu Nai, supreme commander of grain transport, saying they should be demoted or dismissed; many of them had long-standing reputations. Ji ultimately secured an inner imperial order approving the proposal, and the memorial was never sent to the Ministry of Personnel. Since Shu was being prevented from doing his job, he submitted a formal memorial begging to leave, but the request was refused. When Shaanxi needed a grand coordinator, Shu recommended Xiao Zhen, Administration Commissioner of Henan. The emperor ordered him to recommend someone else, but Shu memorialized firmly: "Your Majesty did not deem me unworthy, and entrusted me with the Ministry of Personnel. If the man I recommend proves ineffective, the fault is mine. How does Your Majesty know that Zhen lacks ability and reject him? This must be because some close attendant has someone else in mind. I cannot read the direction of the wind and bend to it merely to secure my salary and position. And since Your Majesty considers Zhen unusable, that means I too am unusable; I beg to retire." The emperor finally appointed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 時言官多稱恕賢且老，不當任劇職，宜置內閣參大政。

translations.literal: Censors then often said Shu was worthy and old and should not bear heavy duties but be placed in the Grand Secretariat to counsel on great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists urged that Shu, virtuous and aged, was unfit for taxing posts and should join the Grand Secretariat to guide state policy.

sentences.zh: 最後，南京御史吳泰等復言之。

translations.literal: Finally Nanjing censor Wu Tai and others raised it again.
translations.idiomatic: At last Wu Tai, a Nanjing censor, and others repeated the plea.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕用蹇義、王直故事，官恕吏部，有謀議未嘗不聽，何必內閣也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I follow the precedents of Jian Yi and Wang Zhi and appoint Shu to the Ministry of Personnel; whenever he has counsel or plans I have never failed to listen. Why must he be in the Grand Secretariat?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "As with Jian Yi and Wang Zhi, I have placed Shu in the Ministry of Personnel, and whenever he has advice I listen. Why insist on the inner cabinet?"

sentences.zh: 恕嘗侍經筵，見帝困熱暑，請依故事大寒暑暫停，仍進講義於宮中。

translations.literal: Once, attending the Classics lecture, he saw the emperor oppressed by summer heat and asked, according to precedent, to suspend lectures in extreme cold or heat while continuing instruction within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: During a Classics lecture he noticed the emperor suffering in the heat and, citing precedent, asked to suspend outdoor lectures in bitter cold or blazing heat while continuing instruction inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 進士董傑、御史湯鼐、給事中韓重等遂交章論駁，恕待罪請解職，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Jinshi Dong Jie, censor Tang Nai, and supervising secretary Han Zhong and others then submitted joint memorials attacking him; Shu asked leave to resign and was comforted with a gracious edict refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jie, Tang Nai, Han Zhong, and others attacked him in concert; Shu offered to resign but received a kind edict keeping him in office.

sentences.zh: 恕上言：「臣蒙國厚恩，日夕思報。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: 'I have received great grace from the state and think of repayment day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote: 'The dynasty has heaped favor on me, and I ponder how to repay it from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 人見陛下任臣過重，遂望臣太深，欲臣盡取朝政更張之，如宋司馬光故事。

translations.literal: People see Your Majesty burden me too heavily and therefore expect too much—that I should overhaul all court policy like Song Sima Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Your Majesty trust me so deeply, many expect me to remake every policy as Sima Guang did in the Song.

sentences.zh: 無論臣才遠不及光，即今亦豈元祐時。

translations.literal: Apart from my talent falling far short of Guang's, is this even the Yuanyou era?
translations.idiomatic: Even setting aside how far I fall short of Guang, this is hardly the Yuanyou age.

sentences.zh: 且六卿分職，各有攸司，臣豈敢越而謀之。

translations.literal: Moreover the six ministries each have its charge; how dare I overstep and plot for them?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, each of the six ministries has its domain; how could I meddle in them all?

sentences.zh: 但傑等責臣良是，臣無所逃罪，惟乞放還。」。

translations.literal: Yet Jie and the others are right to reprove me; I have no escape from blame and beg only to be sent home."
translations.idiomatic: Jie and the rest are justified in rebuking me; I cannot evade fault and ask only to retire."

sentences.zh: 帝復優詔勉留之。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued a gracious edict urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Again the throne sent a kindly edict urging him to remain.

sentences.zh: 恕感激眷遇，益以身任國事。

translations.literal: Grateful for the favor, he threw himself still more into state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the emperor's trust, he devoted himself still more fully to public business.

sentences.zh: 方以疾在告，聞帝頗擢用宦官，至有賜蟒衣給莊田者，具疏切諫。

translations.literal: While ill and on leave he heard that the emperor was promoting eunuchs, even granting python robes and manor lands; he submitted a sharp comprehensive memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Though on sick leave he learned the emperor was elevating eunuchs—even giving python robes and estates—and wrote a stern comprehensive remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 中官黃順請起復匠官潘俊供役，恕言不可以小臣壞重典。

translations.literal: The eunuch Huang Shun asked to recall the artisan Pan Jun from mourning for service; Shu said a minor official must not be allowed to break a major statute.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Shun sought to recall craftsman Pan Jun from mourning, Shu protested that petty servants must not overturn solemn rites.

sentences.zh: 再執奏，竟報許。

translations.literal: He argued twice; permission was granted anyway.
translations.idiomatic: He argued twice, yet approval still came down.

sentences.zh: 劉吉既憾恕，吉所陷壽州知州劉概及言官周纮、張昺、湯鼐、姜綰等，恕又抗章力救，吉以是益恨，乃合私人魏璋等共排之。

translations.literal: Liu Ji already resented Shu; for the cases of Shouzhou prefect Liu Gai and the remonstrators Zhou Hong, Zhang Bing, Tang Nai, Jiang Wan, and others whom Ji had trapped, Shu again fought with bold memorials, and Ji hated him the more and joined his partisans Wei Zhang and others to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji already bore a grudge; when Ji had ruined Liu Gai, prefect of Shouzhou, and censors Zhou Hong, Zhang Bing, Tang Nai, Jiang Wan, and others, Shu again defended them boldly, deepening Ji's hatred until Ji and his clients Wei Zhang and the rest combined to oust him.

sentences.zh: 恕先後推用羅明、熊懷、強珍、陳壽、邱鼐、白思明等，鹹諷璋等糾駁。

translations.literal: Men Shu had promoted—Luo Ming, Xiong Huai, Qiang Zhen, Chen Shou, Qiu Nai, Bai Siming, and others—were all attacked by Zhang and his fellows with sarcastic memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials Shu had advanced—Luo Ming, Xiong Huai, Qiang Zhen, Chen Shou, Qiu Nai, Bai Siming—were mocked and impeached by Zhang's faction.

sentences.zh: 恕知誌不得行，連章求去。

translations.literal: Knowing his aims could not prevail, Shu repeatedly asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his plans blocked, Shu petitioned again and again to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝輒慰留，且以其老特免午朝，遇大風雨雪，早朝亦免。

translations.literal: The emperor always comforted him and kept him, and because of his age specially excused him from the noon audience; in great wind, rain, or snow he was excused from the early audience as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always soothed him and held him back; owing to his age he was freed from the noon levee, and in foul weather from the dawn audience too.

sentences.zh: 徽王見沛乞歸德州田，已得旨。

translations.literal: Prince of Hui Xianjian begged to recover his lands at Dezhou and had already received approval.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Hui had petitioned to reclaim his estates at Dezhou and already held an edict.

sentences.zh: 恕言王國懿親，不當爭尺寸地，使小民失業，帝婉辭報焉。

translations.literal: Shu said a prince of the blood should not wrangle over inches of soil and deprive common people of their livelihood; the emperor answered with mild words.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued that an imperial kinsman ought not fight over scraps of land and ruin peasants; the emperor replied with gentle excuses.

sentences.zh: 盧溝橋成，中官李興乞進文思院副使潘俊等官。

translations.literal: When the Lugou Bridge was completed, the eunuch Li Xing asked promotions for Pan Jun and others of the Wensi Court.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lugou Bridge was finished, the eunuch Li Xing sought offices for Pan Jun and fellow artisans of the Wensi Court.

sentences.zh: 恕言：「營造常職，安得錄功。

translations.literal: Shu said: "Construction is a regular duty; how can merit be recorded for it?
translations.idiomatic: Shu objected: "Building works are ordinary duties. How can they earn recorded merit?

sentences.zh: 成化季始有此事，陛下初政幸已革汰，奈何復行？

translations.literal: Such practices began only at the end of the Chenghua reign; Your Majesty's early rule fortunately abolished them—why revive them now?
translations.idiomatic: This began only in the late Chenghua years; Your Majesty's first reforms had swept it away—why bring it back?

sentences.zh: 且山陵大工未聞升職，援例奏乞，將何詞拒之？」

translations.literal: Moreover, for the great work on the imperial tombs no promotions have been heard of; if others cite this precedent and petition, what words will refuse them?"
translations.idiomatic: And for the tomb works no one has been promoted; once others cite this precedent, how will you turn them away?"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The throne took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 已，修京城河橋，帝復從興請授四人官，許五人冠帶。

translations.literal: Later, when the capital moat bridges were repaired, the emperor again granted offices to four men at Xing's request and allowed five others to wear official insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital river bridges were rebuilt, the emperor again gave four men posts at Li Xing's plea and let five wear court insignia.

sentences.zh: 恕執奏，不從，再疏爭曰：「臣職掌銓選，義當盡言，而再疏莫回天聽，以為業已許之不可易。

translations.literal: Shu insisted in memorials, but this was not followed; he again submitted a memorial disputing it, saying: "Your servant is in charge of personnel selection and by duty must speak fully, yet two memorials have not turned the heavenly hearing, because it is thought that what has already been promised cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pressed his case in vain and wrote again: "I hold responsibility for appointments and must speak out, yet two memorials have failed to move the throne, as though a promise once made cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 夫事求其當，設未當，雖十易何害。

translations.literal: Matters should be judged for their rightness; if they are not right, what harm in changing them ten times?
translations.idiomatic: One should do what is right; if a decision is wrong, why fear changing it even ten times?

sentences.zh: 不然，流弊有不可救者。」

translations.literal: Otherwise abuses will arise that cannot be remedied."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise evils will spread beyond repair."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The reply merely acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The court noted his memorial without acting.

sentences.zh: 先後以災異條七事，以星變陳二十事，鹹切時弊。

translations.literal: He successively set forth seven matters in response to disasters and twenty in response to astral anomalies, all cutting at the abuses of the day.
translations.idiomatic: On calamities he listed seven reforms and on celestial warnings twenty, each striking at current abuses.

sentences.zh: 壽寧伯張巒請勛號、誥券。

translations.literal: The Earl of Shouning, Zhang Luan, asked for an honorary title and patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Luan, Earl of Shouning, petitioned for a meritorious title and patent.

sentences.zh: 恕言：「錢、王兩太后正位中宮數十年，錢承宗、王源始邀封爵。

translations.literal: Shu said: "Empresses Qian and Wang held the central palace in proper position for several decades, yet Qian Chengzong and Wang Yuan only then sought enfeoffed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Shu argued: "Empresses Qian and Wang occupied the central palace for decades before their kinsmen Qian Chengzong and Wang Yuan sought noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 今皇后立甫三年，巒已封伯。

translations.literal: The present empress has stood only three years, yet Luan is already made an earl.
translations.idiomatic: The current empress has been enthroned but three years, and Luan is already an earl.

sentences.zh: 遽有此請，累聖德，不可許。」

translations.literal: To make this request so suddenly burdens the sage virtue and must not be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Such haste will stain the emperor's reputation and must be refused."

sentences.zh: 通政經歷高祿，巒妹婿也，超遷本司參議。

translations.literal: Gao Lu, a bureau experience officer in the Office of Transmission, was Luan's brother-in-law and was promoted over the usual steps to assistant administrator of that office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu of the Transmission Office, Luan's brother-in-law, leapt to assistant administrator by favor.

sentences.zh: 恕言：「天下之官以待天下之士，勿私貴戚，妨公議。」

translations.literal: Shu said: "All offices under Heaven are for all scholars under Heaven; do not favor noble relatives privately and obstruct public judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote: "State posts belong to the worthy men of the realm; do not favor noble in-laws and block fair judgment."

sentences.zh: 中旨以次等禦醫徐生超補院判，恕請選上考者，不納。

translations.literal: An imperial order promoted the third-rank court physician Xu Sheng to vice director of the Medical Institute; Shu asked that top examinees be chosen instead, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: By secret edict Xu Sheng, a third-grade physician, was made vice director; Shu demanded candidates of highest merit and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 文華殿中書舍人杜昌等夤緣遷秩，禦醫王玉自陳乞進官，恕皆力爭寢之。

translations.literal: Du Chang and others of the Wenhua Hall secretariat sought rank by pull, and court physician Wang Yu begged promotion on his own—Shu fought each case until they were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chang of the Wenhua secretariat and physician Wang Yu all sought advancement by favor; Shu contested every case until they were dropped.

sentences.zh: 是時劉吉已罷，而邱濬入閣，亦與恕不相能。

translations.literal: By then Liu Ji had already left office, but Qiu Jun entered the Grand Secretariat and likewise could not work with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji was gone, yet Qiu Jun joined the cabinet and was no friend to Shu either.

sentences.zh: 初，濬以禮部尚書掌詹事，與恕同為太子太保。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun was Minister of Rites directing the Heir Apparent's household, he and Shu were both Junior Guardians of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had been Minister of Rites and tutor to the heir, sharing with Shu the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 恕長六卿，位濬上。

translations.literal: Shu, as senior among the six ministries, ranked above Jun.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the six ministries Shu outranked him.

sentences.zh: 及濬入閣，恕以吏部弗讓也，濬由是不悅。

translations.literal: When Jun entered the cabinet, Shu as Minister of Personnel would not yield precedence, and Jun took offense.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jun entered the cabinet Shu, heading Personnel, refused to defer, and Jun resented it.

sentences.zh: 恕考察天下庶官，已黜而濬調旨留之者九十余人。

translations.literal: Shu had reviewed officials throughout the realm and dismissed many; Jun by secret order kept more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's nationwide review had dismissed scores of officials, yet Jun secured edicts retaining over ninety.

sentences.zh: 恕屢爭不能得，因力求罷，不許。

translations.literal: Shu argued repeatedly in vain and therefore pressed hard to resign, but was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu protested again and again without success and begged to retire, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 太醫院判劉文泰者，故往來濬家以救遷官，為恕所沮，銜恕甚。

translations.literal: Liu Wentai, vice director of the Imperial Medical Institute, had frequented Jun's house to buy promotion and was blocked by Shu; he hated Shu deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Liu Wentai had trafficked with Jun for office and was stopped by Shu, who earned his bitter hatred.

sentences.zh: 恕裏居日，嘗屬人作傳，鏤板以行。

translations.literal: While living at home Shu once had someone write a biography and had it carved for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement Shu had a biography written and printed for distribution.

sentences.zh: 濬謂其沽直謗君，上聞罪且不小。

translations.literal: Jun said he was trading on integrity to slander the ruler and that the crime could hardly be small.
translations.idiomatic: Jun charged that he peddled righteousness to defame the throne—a grave offense.

sentences.zh: 文泰心動，乃自為奏草，示除名都御史吳禎潤色之。

translations.literal: Wentai's heart stirred; he drafted an impeachment himself and had Wu Zhen, a dismissed censor, polish it.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai then composed an accusation and asked the disgraced censor Wu Zhen to refine it.

sentences.zh: 訐恕變亂選法。

translations.literal: It charged Shu with corrupting selection law.
translations.idiomatic: It accused Shu of perverting appointment regulations.

sentences.zh: 且傳中自比伊、周，於奏疏留中者，概雲不報。

translations.literal: The biography also compared him to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and for memorials left undecided it uniformly said 'no reply.'
translations.idiomatic: It claimed the book likened him to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou and marked withheld memorials simply as 'no response.'

sentences.zh: 以彰先帝拒諫，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: This was said to expose the late emperor's rejection of remonstrance and showed lack of ministerial propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Thus it alleged he exposed the previous emperor's refusal of counsel and violated a subject's duty.

sentences.zh: 欲中以奇禍。

translations.literal: They intended to trap him in a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: They aimed to destroy him with a fatal charge.

sentences.zh: 恕以奏出濬指，抗言：「臣傳作於成化二十年，致仕在二十二年，非有望於先帝也。

translations.literal: Shu recognized that the memorial came from Jun and spoke firmly, saying: "Your servant's book was written in the twentieth year of Chenghua, and I retired in the twenty-second; it was not because I hoped for anything from the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu recognized Jun's hand in the memorial and replied firmly: "My book was written in Chenghua 20, and I retired in Chenghua 22; I was not seeking anything from the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 且傳中所載，皆足昭先帝納諫之美，何名彰過。

translations.literal: What the biography records only shows the late emperor's grace in accepting remonstrance; how is that exposing faults?
translations.idiomatic: Its pages praise the late emperor for heeding counsel—how does that shame him?

sentences.zh: 文泰無賴小人，此必有老於文學多陰謀者主之。」

translations.literal: Wentai is a worthless rogue; this must have been directed by some old hand skilled in letters and full of dark schemes."
translations.idiomatic: Wentai is a base scoundrel; some veteran of polished writing and dark plots must be behind this."

sentences.zh: 帝下文泰錦衣獄，鞫之得實，因請逮濬、恕及禎對簿。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Wentai to the Brocade Guard prison; inquiry proved the facts, and he asked that Jun, Shu, and Zhen be brought to face trial.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai was jailed in the Brocade Guard; the truth emerged and he asked to try Jun, Shu, and Zhen together.

sentences.zh: 帝心不悅恕，乃貶文泰禦醫。

translations.literal: The emperor, already displeased with Shu, demoted Wentai to court physician.
translations.idiomatic: Disliking Shu, the emperor only reduced Wentai to physician.

sentences.zh: 責恕沽名，焚所鏤版。

translations.literal: He rebuked Shu for trading on fame and ordered the printed blocks burned.
translations.idiomatic: He scolded Shu for vainglory and burned the blocks.

sentences.zh: 置濬不問。

translations.literal: Jun was left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went untouched.

sentences.zh: 恕再疏請辨理，不從，遂力求去。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized again asking for a hearing and was refused; he then pressed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pleaded for a formal hearing, was denied, and insisted on resigning.

sentences.zh: 聽馳驛歸，不賜敕，月廩、歲隸亦頗減。

translations.literal: He was allowed post horses home but given no farewell edict; his monthly grain and yearly retainers were also much reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the relay home without a parting decree, and his stipends were sharply cut.

sentences.zh: 廷論以是不直濬。

translations.literal: Court opinion therefore held Jun in the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion turned against Jun.

sentences.zh: 及濬卒，文泰往吊，濬妻叱之出曰：「以若故，使相公齮王公，負不義名，何吊為！」

translations.literal: When Jun died, Wentai went to mourn; Jun's wife scolded him and drove him out, saying: "Because of you, my lord slandered Lord Wang and bears an unrighteous name. What are you mourning for?"
translations.idiomatic: At Jun's death Wentai came to condole, but Jun's wife expelled him: "Because of you, my husband attacked Lord Wang and earned a name for unrighteousness. What right have you to mourn?"

sentences.zh: 恕揚歷中外四十余年，剛正清嚴，始終一致。

translations.literal: Shu served inside and outside the court for more than forty years, upright, stern, and pure from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years in central and local posts Shu was fierce, honest, and consistent.

sentences.zh: 所引薦耿裕、彭韶、何喬新、周經、李敏、張悅、倪嶽、劉大夏、戴珊、章懋等，皆一時名臣。

translations.literal: Those he recommended—Geng Yu, Peng Shao, He Qiaoxin, Zhou Jing, Li Min, Zhang Yue, Ni Yue, Liu Daxia, Dai Shan, Zhang Mao, and others—were all leading ministers of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His protégés Geng Yu, Peng Shao, He Qiaoxin, Zhou Jing, Li Min, Zhang Yue, Ni Yue, Liu Daxia, Dai Shan, Zhang Mao, and the rest became pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 他賢才久廢草澤者，拔擢之恐後。

translations.literal: Other worthy men long abandoned in obscurity he raised without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Talents languishing in the wilds he promoted as fast as he could find them.

sentences.zh: 弘治二十年間，眾正盈朝，職業修理，號為極盛者，恕力也。

translations.literal: The twenty years of Hongzhi, when upright men filled the court and every office was put in order—the age called most flourishing—were Shu's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi's golden age, when the court brimmed with integrity and government ran smoothly, was his legacy.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，遣行人賫敕存問，賚羊酒，益廩隸，且諭以讜論無隱。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor succeeded, he sent an envoy with an edict of inquiry, sheep and wine, increased stipends, and orders to speak without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong's accession brought an envoy with gifts, richer pensions, and a command to speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 恕陳國家大政數事，帝優詔報之。

translations.literal: Shu set forth several great policies of state and received a gracious reply.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out major policies and won a kindly edict in answer.

sentences.zh: 正德三年四月卒，年九十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Zhengde he died at ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Zhengde 3, aged ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 平居食啖兼人，卒之日小減。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he ate enough for several men, but on the day of death he ate somewhat less.
translations.idiomatic: A hearty eater all his life, he took only a little less on his last day.

sentences.zh: 閉戶獨坐，忽有聲若雷，白氣瀰漫，瞰之瞑矣。

translations.literal: Sitting alone behind closed doors, he suddenly heard a sound like thunder; white vapor filled the room, and when they looked in he had closed his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Alone behind closed doors he heard thunder; mist whitened the chamber, and he was gone.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，輟朝，贈特進左柱國太師，謚端毅。

translations.literal: When word came, court mourning was suspended; he was posthumously made Special Advance Left Pillar of State and Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Duanyi.
translations.idiomatic: The court halted audiences and enfeoffed him posthumously as Grand Preceptor, Left Pillar of State, with the temple name Duanyi.

sentences.zh: 五子、十三孫，多賢且顯。

translations.literal: Of five sons and thirteen grandsons, many were worthy and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons and thirteen grandsons, most of them talented and eminent.

sentences.zh: 少子承裕，字天宇。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chengyu, styled Tianyu.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest, Chengyu, courtesy name Tianyu.

sentences.zh: 七歲能詩，弱冠著《太極動靜圖說》。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose poetry; in early manhood he wrote 'On the Movement and Stillness of the Supreme Ultimate.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote verse at seven and in youth authored a treatise on the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 恕官吏部，令日接賓客，以是周知天下賢才，選用無不當。

translations.literal: When Shu was Minister of Personnel he had him receive guests daily, and thus came to know all worthy men of the realm and appoint none amiss.
translations.idiomatic: While Shu headed Personnel he had Chengyu greet visitors daily, learning every talent in the land.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Hongzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 恕致政，承裕即告歸侍養。

translations.literal: When Shu retired, Chengyu at once asked leave to return and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: On Shu's retirement Chengyu went home to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 起授兵科給事中，出理山東、河南屯田。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was made supervising secretary of the Bureau of War and sent to administer military colonies in Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed war supervising secretary and oversaw garrison farms in Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 減登、萊糧額，三畝征一斗，還青州、彰德軍田先賜王府者三百六十余頃。

translations.literal: He reduced the grain quota for Deng and Lai, levying one dou per three mu, and returned more than 360 qing of fields in Qingzhou and Zhangde earlier granted to princely houses.
translations.idiomatic: He cut Deng and Lai taxes to one dou per three mu and restored 360-odd qing in Qingzhou and Zhangde from princely grants.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，屢遷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: Under Wuzong he rose repeatedly to chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong he advanced to chief personnel supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以言事忤劉瑾，罰米輸塞上。

translations.literal: For remonstrance he offended Liu Jin and was fined grain to be delivered on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His frank memorials angered Liu Jin, who fined him grain for the border.

sentences.zh: 再遷太仆卿。

translations.literal: He was later promoted to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年累官南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing he rose to Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiajing 6 he was Nanjing Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 清逋稅一百七十萬石，積羨銀四萬八千余兩。

translations.literal: He cleared 1.7 million shi of back taxes and accumulated 48,000-odd taels of surplus silver.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered 1.7 million shi of arrears and banked over 48,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 帝手書「清平正直」褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in his own hand 'Pure, upright, and honest' to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote 'Pure, level, upright, and straight' in praise.

sentences.zh: 在部三年，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served three years, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚康僖。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, temple name Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 马文升

translations.literal: Ma Wensheng
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wensheng

sentences.zh: 馬文升，字負圖，鈞州人。

translations.literal: Ma Wensheng, styled Futian, was a native of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wensheng, courtesy name Futian, came from Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 貌瑰奇多力。

translations.literal: His appearance was striking and he possessed great strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in looks and unusually strong.

sentences.zh: 登景泰二年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Jingtai and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Jingtai 2, he became a censor.

sentences.zh: 歷按山西、湖廣，風裁甚著。

translations.literal: He toured as investigating censor in Shanxi and Huguang, where his moral authority was conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Shanxi and Huguang he won fame for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 還領諸道章奏。

translations.literal: On return he took charge of memorials from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he handled memorials from every province.

sentences.zh: 母喪除，超遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother he was promoted over the usual steps to Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he leapt to Fujian Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化初，召為南京大理卿，以父喪歸。

translations.literal: In the early Chenghua reign he was summoned as Nanjing Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review but returned home for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he was called to be Nanjing Chief Justice, then left for his father's funeral.

sentences.zh: 滿四之亂，陜西巡撫陳價下吏，即家起文升右副都御史代價。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Man Si, Shaanxi grand coordinator Chen Jia was imprisoned and Wensheng was raised from home as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace Jia.
translations.idiomatic: When Man Si rebelled, coordinator Chen Jia was jailed and Wensheng was summoned from home as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 馳至軍，與總督項忠討平之。

translations.literal: He galloped to the army and with Governor Xiang Zhong pacified the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to camp and with Governor Xiang Zhong crushed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事具忠傳。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in Zhong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign is told fully in Zhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 錄功進左副都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted Left Vice Censor-in-Chief while remaining grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded, he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and kept the coordinator's post.

sentences.zh: 文升數條奏便宜，務選將練兵，修安邊營至鐵鞭城烽堠，剪除劇賊。

translations.literal: Wensheng repeatedly memorialized practical measures, striving to choose generals and drill troops, repair frontier camps as far as the Iron Whip City beacon towers, and eliminate fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He urged choosing generals, drilling soldiers, rebuilding frontier posts to Iron Whip City, and wiping out bandits.

sentences.zh: 西固番族不即命者悉滅之。

translations.literal: Tribal groups of Xigu who would not obey were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Disobedient Xigu tribes were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 修茶政，易番馬八千有奇，以給士卒。

translations.literal: He reformed the tea trade, exchanging more than eight thousand frontier horses to supply the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tea policy reforms brought eight thousand-odd horses for the army.

sentences.zh: 振鞏昌、臨洮饑民，撫安流移。

translations.literal: He relieved famine in Gongchang and Lintao and settled displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: He fed Gongchang and Lintao in famine and resettled refugees.

sentences.zh: 績甚著。

translations.literal: His achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: His record was brilliant.

sentences.zh: 是時，孛羅忽、滿都魯、乚加思蘭比歲犯邊。

translations.literal: At that time Boluohu, Mandulur, and Yibasanjin raided the border year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Boluohu, Mandulur, and Yibasanjin attacked annually.

sentences.zh: 文升請駐兵韋州，而設伏諸堡待之。

translations.literal: Wensheng asked to station troops at Weizhou and set ambushes in the forts to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Weizhou and laid ambushes along the forts.

sentences.zh: 遂敗寇黑水口，擒其平章叠烈孫，又敗之湯羊嶺，斬首二百，名其嶺曰：「得勝坡」，勒石紀之而還。

translations.literal: He then defeated the raiders at Heishui Pass, capturing their pingzhang Tieliesun, and defeated them again at Tangyang Ridge, taking two hundred heads; he named the ridge "Slope of Victory," carved a stone to record it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the raiders at Heishui Pass and captured their pingzhang Tieliesun, then defeated them again at Tangyang Ridge, taking two hundred heads; he named the ridge "Victory Slope," set up a stele to commemorate it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文升軍功甚盛，奏捷不為誇張，中亦無主之者，以是賞薄。

translations.literal: Wensheng's military merit was great; his victory reports were not exaggerated, yet he had no patron at court and rewards were thin.
translations.idiomatic: Though his victories were real and modestly reported, he lacked court patrons and was meagerly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 至九年冬，總制王越以大捷奏，文升亦遣子琇報功。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year Governor Wang Yue reported a great victory and Wensheng sent his son Xiu to report merit as well.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year 9 Wang Yue claimed a great victory and Wensheng sent his son Xiu to report too.

sentences.zh: 廷臣勘奏不實，坐停俸三月。

translations.literal: Court investigators found the accounts false and both were penalized with three months' salary withheld.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators ruled the claims false and docked three months' pay.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，代越總制三邊軍務，尋入為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he replaced Yue as overall commander of the Three Frontiers and soon entered the capital as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 11 he succeeded Yue commanding the Three Frontiers, then became Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，整飭遼東軍務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year he reorganized Liaodong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year's eighth month he put Liaodong forces in order.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳鉞貪而狡，將士小過輒罰馬，馬價騰踴。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Chen Yue was greedy and cunning; for small faults he fined officers in horses until horse prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinator Chen Yue, greedy and sly, fined minor offenses in horses until prices skyrocketed.

sentences.zh: 文升上邊計十五事，因請禁之，鉞由是嗛文升。

translations.literal: Wensheng submitted fifteen frontier measures and asked to forbid this; Yue therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng proposed fifteen frontier reforms banning the practice, and Yue hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 文升還部轉左。

translations.literal: Wensheng returned to the ministry and was shifted to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the ministry he moved to the left vice post.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，鉞以掩殺冒功激變，中官汪直欲自往定之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year Yue provoked mutiny by claiming false kills for merit, and the eunuch Wang Zhi wished to go pacify it himself.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 14 Yue's false battle honors sparked mutiny, and eunuch Wang Zhi wanted to lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝令司禮太監懷恩等七人詣內閣會兵部議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered seven men including the Director of Ceremonials Huai En to meet the Grand Secretariat and the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Seven eunuchs led by Huai En were sent to consult the cabinet and War Ministry.

sentences.zh: 恩欲遣大臣往撫，以沮直行。

translations.literal: En wished to dispatch a senior minister to pacify the region and thereby block Zhi's expedition.
translations.idiomatic: En hoped a grand minister's mission would stop Zhi from going.

sentences.zh: 文升疾應曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Wensheng, though ill, answered at once: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Though ill, Wensheng instantly said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 恩入白，帝即命文升往。

translations.literal: En reported inside, and the emperor at once ordered Wensheng to go.
translations.idiomatic: En spoke to the emperor, who immediately dispatched Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 直不悅，欲令其私人王英與俱，文升謝絕之。

translations.literal: Zhi was displeased and wished his client Wang Ying to go along; Wensheng declined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wanted his man Wang Ying to accompany him; Wensheng refused.

sentences.zh: 疾馳至鎮，宣璽書撫慰，無不聽撫者。

translations.literal: He galloped to the post, proclaimed the imperial edict of comfort, and none who heard the pacification refused it.
translations.idiomatic: Racing to the frontier he proclaimed the comforting edict, and all submitted to pacification.

sentences.zh: 又請前以也先亂失授官璽書者十余人，得襲官。

translations.literal: He also asked that more than ten men who had lost appointment patents in the chaos of Esen's rebellion be allowed to inherit office.
translations.idiomatic: He secured hereditary office for a dozen men who lost patents in Esen's turmoil.

sentences.zh: 事定，直欲攘其功，請於帝，挾王英馳至開原，再下令招撫。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Zhi wished to seize the credit and begged the emperor; taking Wang Ying he galloped to Kaiyuan and again issued orders of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then tried to steal the credit, rushed with Wang Ying to Kaiyuan, and reissued pacification orders.

sentences.zh: 文升乃推功與直，然直內慚。

translations.literal: Wensheng yielded the merit to Zhi, yet Zhi felt inward shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng deferred the glory to Zhi, though Zhi was secretly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 文升又與直抗禮，奴視其左右，直益不喜。

translations.literal: Wensheng also treated Zhi as an equal in ceremony and looked on Zhi's attendants as servants; Zhi grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He met Zhi as an equal and treated Zhi's followers like slaves, deepening the rift.

sentences.zh: 而陳鉞益諂事直，得直歡。

translations.literal: Chen Yue meanwhile flattered Zhi the more and won his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue fawned on Zhi and won his favor.

sentences.zh: 日夜譖文升，思中之未有以發也。

translations.literal: Day and night he slandered Wensheng, seeking a chance to strike him but finding none.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered Wensheng day and night, seeking a pretext in vain.

sentences.zh: 文升還，賜牢醴。

translations.literal: Wensheng returned and was granted a feast of meat and wine.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the court rewarded him with meat and wine.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以遼東屢失事，遣直偕定西侯蔣琬、尚書林聰等按之。

translations.literal: The next spring, because Liaodong had repeatedly failed in duty, Zhi was sent with the Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan, Minister Lin Cong, and others to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring, after Liaodong's repeated failures, Zhi went with Jiang Wan and Lin Cong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 會余子俊劾鉞，鉞疑出文升意，傾之益急。

translations.literal: When Yu Zijun impeached Yue, Yue suspected Wensheng's hand and attacked him all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun impeached Yue, who blamed Wensheng and redoubled his attacks.

sentences.zh: 直因奏文升行事乖方，禁邊人市農器，致怨叛。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized that Wensheng's conduct was perverse, forbidding frontier people to buy farm tools and causing resentment and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi charged that Wensheng had forbidden farm tools on the frontier, provoking revolt.

sentences.zh: 乃下文升詔獄，謫戍重慶衛。

translations.literal: Wensheng was sent to the imperial prison and banished to garrison Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed and exiled to Chongqing guard.

sentences.zh: 直既傾文升，則與鉞大發兵激功，鉞以是驟遷至尚書。

translations.literal: Once Zhi had overthrown Wensheng, he and Yue launched great campaigns for merit, and Yue swiftly rose to minister.
translations.idiomatic: With Wensheng gone, Zhi and Yue waged aggressive wars for glory, and Yue vaulted to minister.

sentences.zh: 十九年，直敗，文升復官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Zhi fell, and Wensheng was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi fell in year 19, Wensheng was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 明年起為左副都御史巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: The next year he was raised as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 文升凡三至遼，軍民聞其來皆鼓舞。

translations.literal: Wensheng went to Liaodong three times in all; soldiers and civilians cheered at his coming.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he went to Liaodong, and each arrival was met with joy.

sentences.zh: 益禁抑中官、總兵，使不得朘削，眾益大喜。

translations.literal: He further restrained eunuchs and regional commanders from squeezing the people, and the masses rejoiced still more.
translations.idiomatic: He barred eunuchs and commanders from extortion, to universal delight.

sentences.zh: 二十一年進右都御史，總督漕運。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted Right Censor-in-Chief and overall director of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he became Right Censor-in-Chief and grain transport director.

sentences.zh: 淮、徐、和饑，移江南糧十萬石、鹽價銀五萬兩振之。

translations.literal: Huai, Xu, and He suffered famine; he moved a hundred thousand shi of Jiangnan grain and fifty thousand taels of salt money for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Huai, Xu, and He; he shipped 100,000 shi of Jiangnan grain and 50,000 taels in salt funds.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，召為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter he was summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was called to be Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，以李孜省譖，調南京。

translations.literal: The next year, on Li Zisheng's slander, he was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Li Zisheng's slander sent him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded, he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong summoned him as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年上言：「憲宗朝，嶽鎮海瀆諸廟，用方士言置石函，周以符篆，貯金書道經、金銀錢、寶石及五谷為厭勝具，宜毀。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he memorialized: "In the Xianzong reign, at the temples of mountains, marches, seas, and waterways, stone caskets were placed on the advice of fangshi, surrounded with talisman script, and filled with golden Daoist scriptures, gold and silver coins, gems, and the five grains as apotropaic objects. They should be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 he memorialized: "Under Xianzong, stone caskets were buried at the state temples of mountains, marches, seas, and waterways on the advice of occult specialists; they were ringed with talismanic writing and filled with golden Daoist scriptures, gold and silver coins, gems, and the five grains as apotropaic objects. They should be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 又上言十五事，悉議行。

translations.literal: He also set forth fifteen matters, all debated and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed fifteen reforms, all adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝耕藉田，教坊以雜戲進。

translations.literal: When the emperor plowed the sacred field, the music bureau presented variety plays.
translations.idiomatic: At the plowing ceremony the entertainment office offered variety shows.

sentences.zh: 文升正色曰：「新天子當使知稼穡艱難，此何為者？」

translations.literal: Wensheng said sternly: "The new Son of Heaven should be made to know the hardships of sowing and reaping. What are these for?"
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng said gravely, "A new emperor should learn the toil of the fields. What are these diversions for?"

sentences.zh: 即斥去。

translations.literal: He immediately had them driven away.
translations.idiomatic: He had them dismissed at once.

sentences.zh: 御史徐瑁、賀霖失承旨下獄。

translations.literal: Censors Xu Wan and He Lin, for failing to receive an edict, were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xu Wan and He Lin were jailed for missing an edict.

sentences.zh: 文升言初政不宜輒罪言官，遂得釋。

translations.literal: Wensheng said that at the start of a reign one should not lightly punish remonstrators, and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that early rule must not punish critics, and they were freed.

sentences.zh: 尋命提督十二團營。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to direct the twelve regimental camps.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the twelve regimental camps.

sentences.zh: 明年，代余子俊為兵部尚書，督團營如故。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced Yu Zijun as Minister of War while keeping command of the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he succeeded Yu Zijun as war minister while retaining the camps.

sentences.zh: 承平既久，兵政廢弛，西北部落時伺塞下。

translations.literal: Long peace had let military affairs decay, and northwestern tribes watched the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had rotted the army while frontier tribes watched for openings.

sentences.zh: 文升嚴核諸將校，黜貪懦者三十余人。

translations.literal: Wensheng strictly reviewed commanders and dismissed more than thirty greedy or cowardly men.
translations.idiomatic: He audited officers and removed over thirty who were greedy or timid.

sentences.zh: 奸人大怨，夜持弓矢伺其門，或作謗書射入東長安門內。

translations.literal: Villains hated him deeply; by night they waited at his gate with bow and arrow, or shot libelous placards into the East Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies lurked at his door with bows or shot slander sheets into the East Chang'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，詔錦衣緝捕，給騎士十二，衛文升出入。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and ordered the Brocade Guard to hunt them down and gave twelve guards to escort Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered arrests and twelve guards to escort him.

sentences.zh: 文升乞休，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Wensheng asked to retire but received a gracious refusal.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to retire but was kindly kept on.

sentences.zh: 小王子以數萬騎牧大同塞下，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: The Little Prince pastured tens of thousands of horses below the Datong frontier, his force menacing.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince herded tens of thousands of horses below Datong, a threatening host.

sentences.zh: 文升以疾在告，帝使中官挾醫視，因就問計。

translations.literal: Wensheng was ill at home; the emperor sent a eunuch with a physician to see him and consult on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at home, he was visited by a eunuch-physician sent to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 文升謂「彼方敗於他部，無能為。

translations.literal: Wensheng said, 'They have just been defeated by another tribe and can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'They were just beaten by another tribe and are harmless.

sentences.zh: 請密為備，而揚聲逼之，必徙去。」

translations.literal: Please secretly prepare defenses, while loudly pressing them; they will surely move away."
translations.idiomatic: Prepare in secret, but make a public show of pressure, and they will surely withdraw."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: It proved so.
translations.idiomatic: So it happened.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，詔起復，再疏辭，不許。

translations.literal: During mourning for his stepmother he was ordered to resume office; he memorialized twice to decline and was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his stepmother, he was ordered back; twice he refused and was overruled.

sentences.zh: 西北別部野乜克力，其長曰亦剌思王，曰滿哥王，曰亦剌因王，各遣使款肅州塞，乞貢且互市。

translations.literal: Of the Yemekli branch in the northwest, the chiefs Yilasi Wang, Mange Wang, and Yilayin Wang each sent envoys to the Suzhou pass seeking tribute and mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern Yemekli chiefs Yilasi, Mange, and Yilayin sought trade and tribute at Suzhou pass.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許進、總兵官劉寧為請，文升言互市可許，入貢不可許，乃卻之。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Xu Jin and regional commander Liu Ning asked approval; Wensheng said markets could be allowed but tribute entries not, and they were refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jin and Liu Ning petitioned; Wensheng allowed trade but refused tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 土魯番既襲執陜巴，而令牙蘭據守哈密，僭稱可汗，侵沙州，迫罕東諸部附己。

translations.literal: Turfan had seized and held Shamba and put Yalan in Hami, styling himself khan, invading Shazhou and forcing Han east tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Turfan held Shamba, garrisoned Yalan in Hami as khan, raided Shazhou, and coerced eastern tribes.

sentences.zh: 文升議，此寇桀驁，不大創終不知畏，宜用漢陳湯故事襲斬之。

translations.literal: Wensheng argued that this bandit was fierce and would not fear without a heavy blow; the Han precedent of Chen Tang's surprise strike should be used.
translations.idiomatic: He urged a Chen Tang-style strike, saying the raiders would heed only force.

sentences.zh: 察指揮楊翥熟番情，召詢以方略。

translations.literal: Seeing Commander Yang Yong of Chaxi knew tribal conditions, he summoned him for plans.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Commander Yang Yong of Chaxi, expert on the tribes.

sentences.zh: 翥備陳罕東至哈密道路，請調罕東兵三千為前鋒，漢兵三千繼之，持數日糧，間道兼程進，可得誌。

translations.literal: Yong detailed the road from Handom east to Hami and asked for three thousand Handom troops as vanguard and three thousand Han troops after, with several days' rations, marching by hidden paths at double speed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong mapped the route and proposed 3,000 Handom scouts plus 3,000 Han troops with swift supplies by secret paths.

sentences.zh: 文升喜，遂請於帝，敕發罕東、赤斤、哈密兵，令副總兵彭清將之，隸巡撫許進往討，果克之，語詳《進傳》。

translations.literal: Wensheng rejoiced and asked the emperor to issue orders mobilizing Handom, Chijin, and Hami troops under Vice Commander Peng Qing, under coordinator Xu Jin; they took the city—the story is in Jin's biography.
