translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; Peng Qing and Xu Jin took Hami, as told in Jin's biography.

sentences.zh: 團營軍不足，請於錦衣及騰驤四衛中選補。

translations.literal: The regimental camps lacked men; he asked to fill them from the Brocade Guard and the four Tengxiang guards.
translations.idiomatic: He sought recruits from the Brocade Guard and Tengxiang guards for the camps.

sentences.zh: 已得請矣，中官寧瑾阻之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted, but the eunuch Ning Jin blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Approval came, yet eunuch Ning Jin obstructed it.

sentences.zh: 文升及兵科蔚春等言詔旨宜信，不納。

translations.literal: Wensheng and the war bureau's Wei Chun said imperial words should be trusted, but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng and Wei Chun insisted edicts must be honored, but were ignored.

sentences.zh: 陜西地大震。

translations.literal: A great earthquake struck Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi suffered a great earthquake.

sentences.zh: 文升言：「此外寇侵淩之兆。

translations.literal: Wensheng said: 'This is a sign of foreign invasion and oppression.
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'This foretells foreign aggression.

sentences.zh: 今火篩方跳梁，而海內民困財竭，將懦兵弱。

translations.literal: Now Huosai is rampant while the realm is exhausted, generals weak and soldiers feeble.
translations.idiomatic: Huosai stirs while the people are drained and the army enfeebled.

sentences.zh: 宜行仁政以養民，講武備以固圉。

translations.literal: Benevolent government should nourish the people and military readiness secure the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Rule with benevolence and strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 節財用，停齋醮，止傳奉冗員，禁奏乞閑地。

translations.literal: Economize spending, halt vegetarian feasts, stop redundant honorary posts, and forbid petitions for idle lands.
translations.idiomatic: Cut expenses, end ritual excess, purge honorary posts, and stop land grabs.

sentences.zh: 日視二朝，以勤庶政。

translations.literal: Attend both daily audiences and diligently handle government.
translations.idiomatic: Hold both daily audiences and work diligently.

sentences.zh: 且撤還陜西織造內臣，振恤被災者家。」

translations.literal: Also recall the Shaanxi weaving eunuchs and relieve the households of those struck by disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Also recall the Shaanxi weaving eunuchs and aid the families of the afflicted."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，內臣立召還。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and the inner eunuchs were recalled at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and recalled the eunuchs immediately.

sentences.zh: 文升為兵部十三年，盡心戎務，於屯田、馬政、邊備、守禦，數條上便宜。

translations.literal: Wensheng served thirteen years in the Ministry of War, devoting himself to military affairs; on garrison farms, horse policy, frontier defense, and guard duties he repeatedly memorialized practical measures.
translations.idiomatic: For thirteen years as war minister he drove military reform—garrison farms, horses, defenses, and guards.

sentences.zh: 國家事當言者，即非職守，亦言無不盡。

translations.literal: Whatever concerned the state, even outside his charge, he spoke without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: On any state matter, even beyond his portfolio, he spoke fully.

sentences.zh: 嘗以太子年及四齡，當早諭教。

translations.literal: He once said that as the heir was already four, early instruction was needed.
translations.idiomatic: He urged early education for the four-year-old heir.

sentences.zh: 請擇醇謹老成知書史如衛聖楊夫人者，保抱扶持，凡言語動止悉導之以正。

translations.literal: He asked to choose sober, careful elders versed in books and history like Lady Yang of Weisheng to nurse and guide him, directing every word and act by the right.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted matrons like Lady Yang of Weisheng to guide the heir's every word and deed.

sentences.zh: 若內庭曲宴，鐘鼓司承應，元宵鰲山，端午競渡諸戲，皆勿令見。

translations.literal: Private inner banquets with the bell office, Lantern Festival turtle hills, Dragon Boat races, and such plays should never be shown him.
translations.idiomatic: He must not see inner revels, lantern displays, or dragon-boat pageants.

sentences.zh: 至於佛、老之教，尤宜屏絕，恐惑眩心誌。

translations.literal: Buddhist and Daoist teachings especially should be barred lest they dazzle his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Daoist rites should be kept away lest they confuse him.

sentences.zh: 山東久旱，浙江及南畿水災，文升請命所司振恤，練士卒以備不虞。

translations.literal: Shandong had long drought and Zhejiang and the southern capital floods; Wensheng asked relief agencies to aid victims and drill troops against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: He sought relief for drought and flood zones and troop drills for crises.

sentences.zh: 帝皆深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor embraced every proposal.

sentences.zh: 民困賦役，文升極陳其害，謂：「今民田十稅四五，其輸邊塞者糧一石費銀一兩以上，豐年用糧八九石方易一兩。

translations.literal: The people were harried by taxes and corvee; Wensheng laid out the harm in full, saying: "Today private fields pay four or five tenths in tax; for grain transported to the frontier, one shi costs more than one tael of silver, and in a good year eight or nine shi of grain are needed to exchange for one tael.
translations.idiomatic: The people were crushed by taxes and labor service, and Wensheng set out the harm in detail: "Today private fields are taxed at forty to fifty percent; grain sent to the frontier costs more than one tael per shi, and even in good years eight or nine shi of grain are needed to obtain one tael.

sentences.zh: 若絲綿布帛之輸京師者，交納之費過於所輸，南方轉漕通州至有三四石致一石者。

translations.literal: Silks and cottons sent to the capital cost more in delivery than in value; southern transport to Tongzhou sometimes takes three or four shi to deliver one.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute cloth costs more to deliver than it is worth; southern grain sometimes loses three shi per one delivered.

sentences.zh: 中州歲役五六萬人治河，山東、河南修塞決口夫不下二十萬，蘇、松治水亦如之。

translations.literal: The central provinces yearly employ fifty or sixty thousand men on the river; Shandong and Henan repair breach works with no fewer than two hundred thousand; Suzhou and Songjiang waterworks likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Millions labor on rivers and dikes in the central plain and south.

sentences.zh: 湖廣建吉、興、岐、雍四王府，江西益、壽二府，山東衡府，通計役夫不下百萬。

translations.literal: Huguang built four princely mansions for Ji, Xing, Qi, and Yong; Jiangxi added Yi and Shou; Shandong the Heng mansion—corvée totaled over a million.
translations.idiomatic: Princely construction in Huguang, Jiangxi, and Shandong alone consumed a million laborers.

sentences.zh: 諸王之國役夫供應亦四十萬。

translations.literal: Princes going to their fiefs required another four hundred thousand for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Princely enfeoffment processions took four hundred thousand more.

sentences.zh: 加以湖廣征蠻，山、陜防邊，供饋餉給軍旅者又不知凡幾。

translations.literal: Add Huguang's campaigns against the Miao, Shan-Shaan frontier defense, and countless army provisions—none know how many.
translations.idiomatic: Add Miao campaigns, frontier garrisons, and army supply—beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 賦重役繁，未有甚於此時者也。

translations.literal: Taxes and corvée have never been heavier than now.
translations.idiomatic: Burden has never been greater.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴敕內外諸司，省煩費，寬力役，毋擅有科率，王府之工宜速竣。

translations.literal: Strictly order all offices to cut waste, ease labor, forbid unauthorized levies, and finish princely construction quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Cut waste, ease labor, ban illegal levies, and finish princely works swiftly.

sentences.zh: 庶令困敝少蘇。

translations.literal: Thus the exhausted may breathe a little.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can the people recover.

sentences.zh: 更乞崇正學，抑邪術，以清聖心；

translations.literal: Further, exalt orthodox learning and suppress heterodox arts to clarify the sacred mind;
translations.idiomatic: Uphold orthodox learning and suppress sorcery to purify the imperial mind;

sentences.zh: 節財用，省工作，以培邦本。」

translations.literal: economize on expenditures and reduce works, in order to strengthen the foundation of the state."
translations.idiomatic: save public wealth and reduce labor projects, so as to strengthen the foundation of the realm."

sentences.zh: 詔下所司詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate in detail.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered detailed review.

sentences.zh: 他所論奏者甚眾。

translations.literal: His other memorials were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He filed countless other memorials.

sentences.zh: 在班列中最為耆碩，帝亦推心任之。

translations.literal: Among the court ranks he was the most senior, and the emperor trusted him wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: He was the eldest statesman and enjoyed the emperor's full trust.

sentences.zh: 自太子太保屢加至少保兼太子太傅，歲時賜賚，諸大臣莫敢望也。

translations.literal: From Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; yearly gifts no other minister dared expect.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to tutor ranks, he received gifts no peer could match.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書屠滽罷，廷推文升。

translations.literal: When Minister of Personnel Tu Fu retired, the court pushed Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Tu Fu left Personnel, the court favored Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 御史魏英等言兵部非文升不可，帝亦以為然。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Ying and others said the Ministry of War could not do without Wensheng, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Censors said War needed Wensheng; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃命倪嶽代滽，而加文升少傅以慰之。

translations.literal: Ni Yue was appointed in Tu's place, and Wensheng was made Junior Tutor to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Yue replaced Tu while Wensheng was made Junior Tutor as consolation.

sentences.zh: 嶽卒，以文升代。

translations.literal: When Yue died, Wensheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ni Yue died, Wensheng took Personnel.

sentences.zh: 南京、鳳陽大風雨壞屋拔木，文升請帝減膳撤樂，修德省愆，禦經筵，絕遊宴；

translations.literal: Great wind and rain in Nanjing and Fengyang destroyed houses and uprooted trees; Wensheng asked the emperor to reduce meals, withdraw music, cultivate virtue and examine faults, attend the Classics lecture, and cease tours and feasts;
translations.idiomatic: Storms wrecked Nanjing and Fengyang; he urged frugal meals, no music, self-examination, Classics study, and an end to revels;

sentences.zh: 停不急務，止額外織造；

translations.literal: 'halt unurgent tasks and stop extra weaving;'
translations.idiomatic: 'halt petty projects and extra weaving;'

sentences.zh: 振饑民，捕盜賊。

translations.literal: 'relieve famine victims and capture bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: 'relieve the hungry and catch bandits.'

sentences.zh: 已，又上吏部職掌十事。

translations.literal: Later he also submitted ten articles on the duties of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted ten rules for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝悉褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 一品九載滿，加少師兼太子太師。

translations.literal: Nine years at the first rank completed, he was made Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years at rank one he became Junior Preceptor and Tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝以將考察，特召文升及都御史戴珊、史琳至暖閣，諭以秉公黜陟。

translations.literal: As an inspection was due, the emperor specially summoned Wensheng and Censors-in-Chief Dai Shan and Shi Lin to the Warm Pavilion and instructed them to dismiss and promote fairly.
translations.idiomatic: Before an inspection he summoned Wensheng, Dai Shan, and Shi Lin to the Warm Pavilion for fair promotions.

sentences.zh: 又以文升年高重聽，再呼告之，命左右掖之下階。

translations.literal: Because Wensheng was old and hard of hearing, he called again to tell him and ordered attendants to support him down the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Finding him deaf with age, the emperor repeated his orders and had attendants help him down.

sentences.zh: 始文升為都御史，王恕在吏部，兩人皆以正直任天下事。

translations.literal: When Wensheng was Censor-in-Chief and Wang Shu was in Personnel, both undertook the world's affairs with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As censor-in-chief alongside Wang Shu in Personnel, both bore the realm's burdens uprightly.

sentences.zh: 疏出，天下傳誦。

translations.literal: When their memorials issued, the realm copied and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorials were copied and read throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 恕去，人望皆歸文升。

translations.literal: When Shu left, public hope all turned to Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu's departure all eyes rested on Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 迨為吏部，年已八十。

translations.literal: When he became Minister of Personnel he was already eighty.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he headed Personnel he was eighty.

sentences.zh: 修髯長眉，遇事侃侃不少衰。

translations.literal: With long beard and brows he spoke forthrightly on affairs without the least decline.
translations.idiomatic: Long-bearded and long-browed, he argued as boldly as ever.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，文升承遺詔請汰傳奉官七百六十三人，命留太仆卿李綸等十七人，余盡汰之。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, Wensheng carried out the testamentary edict asking to dismiss seven hundred sixty-three honorary attendants; the order kept seventeen including Director of the Imperial Stud Li Lun and dismissed the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozong's death Wensheng executed the will to purge 763 honorary attendants, sparing only seventeen including Li Lun.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，禦用監中官王瑞復請用新汰者七人，文升不奉詔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, the eunuch Wang Rui of the Imperial Wardrobe again asked to employ seven newly dismissed men; Wensheng refused the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 eunuch Wang Rui sought to restore seven dismissed men; Wensheng refused.

sentences.zh: 給事中安奎刺得瑞納賄狀，劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary An Kui uncovered Rui's bribe-taking and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary An Kui exposed Rui's bribes and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 瑞恚，誣文升抗旨，更下廷議，皆是文升，帝終不聽。

translations.literal: Rui, enraged, falsely charged Wensheng with defying the edict; the matter went to court debate, all siding with Wensheng, and the emperor in the end did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Rui accused Wensheng of defiance; court debate backed Wensheng and the emperor held firm.

sentences.zh: 文升因乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Wensheng therefore asked to retire and was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to retire but was refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝政已移於中官，文升老，日懷去誌。

translations.literal: By then court power had shifted to eunuchs; Wensheng, old, daily thought of leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Court power lay with eunuchs; the aged Wensheng longed to go home.

sentences.zh: 會兩廣缺總督，文升推兵部侍郎熊繡。

translations.literal: When the two Guangs lacked an overall commander, Wensheng recommended Vice Minister of War Xiong Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Xiong Xiu for the vacant Liang-Guang command.

sentences.zh: 繡怏怏不欲出，其鄉人御史何天衢遂劾文升徇私欺罔。

translations.literal: Xiu was displeased and unwilling to go; his townsman censor He Tianqu then impeached Wensheng for favoritism and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu resented the post; his fellow townsman He Tianqu impeached Wensheng for nepotism.

sentences.zh: 文升連疏求去，許之。

translations.literal: Wensheng memorialized repeatedly to leave and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated pleas won his release.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書、乘傳，月廩歲隸有加。

translations.literal: He was granted a sealed edict and relay transport; monthly grain and yearly retainers were increased.
translations.idiomatic: He received a sealed edict, relay horses, and richer stipends.

sentences.zh: 家居，非事未嘗入州城。

translations.literal: At home he never entered the prefectural city unless on business.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he rarely entered the city except on necessity.

sentences.zh: 語及時事，輒顰蹙不答。

translations.literal: When talk turned to current affairs he only frowned and would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about politics he frowned and stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 居三年，劉瑾亂政，坐文升前用雍泰為朋黨，除其名。

translations.literal: After three years at home, Liu Jin's misrule made Wensheng guilty for earlier employing Yong Tai as a faction member, and his name was struck.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Liu Jin struck his name for having favored Yong Tai.

sentences.zh: 五年六月卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year he died at eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of year 5, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，贈特進光祿大夫、太傅，謚端肅。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed his office was restored; he was posthumously made Special Advance Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored and posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor Duansu.

sentences.zh: 文升有文武才，長於應變，朝端大議往往待之決。

translations.literal: Wensheng had both civil and military talent and excelled in emergencies; great court debates often awaited his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted in civil and military affairs, he settled crises the court could not decide alone.

sentences.zh: 功在邊鎮，外國皆聞其名。

translations.literal: His merit lay on the frontier; foreign states all knew his name.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier service made his name known abroad.

sentences.zh: 尤重氣節，厲廉隅，直道而行。

translations.literal: He especially valued integrity, upheld purity, and walked the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity and walked the straight path.

sentences.zh: 雖遭讒詬，屢起屢仆，迄不少貶。

translations.literal: Though slandered and repeatedly risen and fallen, he was never in the least diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and reversals never bent him.

sentences.zh: 子璁，以鄉貢士待選吏部，文升使請外，曰：「必大臣子而京秩，誰當外者？」

translations.literal: His son Cong, a provincial graduate awaiting selection by the Ministry of Personnel, was made by Wensheng to request an outside post; Wensheng said: "If the sons of great ministers must all hold capital posts, who will serve outside?"
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong, a provincial graduate awaiting appointment by the Ministry of Personnel, was sent by Wensheng to request a provincial post; Wensheng said, "If ministers' sons must all receive capital appointments, who will go outside?"

sentences.zh: 卒後逾年，大盜趙鐩等剽河南，至鈞州，以文升家在，舍之去。

translations.literal: More than a year after his death the great bandit Zhao Zhen and others plundered Henan; reaching Junzhou, because Wensheng's house was there they passed it by.
translations.idiomatic: A year after his death bandits spared Junzhou out of respect for his home.

sentences.zh: 攻泌陽，毀焦芳家，束草若芳像裂之。

translations.literal: Attacking Biyang they destroyed Jiao Fang's house and bound straw like Fang's image and tore it apart.
translations.idiomatic: At Biyang they wrecked Jiao Fang's house and rent a straw effigy of him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，加贈文升左柱國、太師。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing reign Wensheng was further enfeoffed as Left Pillar of State and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jiajing added posthumous rank as Left Pillar and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 刘大夏

translations.literal: Liu Daxia
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daxia

sentences.zh: 劉大夏，字時雍，華容人。

translations.literal: Liu Daxia, styled Shiyong, was a native of Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daxia, courtesy name Shiyong, came from Huarong.

sentences.zh: 父仁宅，由鄉舉知瑞昌縣。

translations.literal: His father Renzhai rose through the provincial examination to be magistrate of Ruichang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renzhai became magistrate of Ruichang via the provincial exam.

sentences.zh: 流民千余家匿山中，邏者索賂不得，誣民反。

translations.literal: More than a thousand displaced households hid in the mountains; patrolmen, denied bribes, accused the people of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand refugees hid in the hills; patrolmen, refused bribes, cried rebellion.

sentences.zh: 眾議加兵。

translations.literal: The crowd proposed sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Officials urged military action.

sentences.zh: 仁宅單騎招之，民爭出訴，遂罷兵，擢廣西副使。

translations.literal: Renzhai went alone on horseback to summon them; the people came out to plead and troops were withdrawn; he was promoted Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhai rode alone to parley; the people submitted and he was made Guangxi vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大夏年二十舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Daxia at twenty came first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Daxia topped the provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 登天順八年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Tianshun and became a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Tianshun 8, he entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 成化初，館試當留，自請試吏。

translations.literal: In early Chenghua, qualifying to remain in the Academy, he asked instead to test himself in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early Chenghua he declined Academy tenure to serve in office.

sentences.zh: 乃除職方主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Bureau of Military Appointments and twice promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Bureau of Military Appointments secretary, then director.

sentences.zh: 明習兵事，曹中宿弊盡革。

translations.literal: Skilled in military affairs, he reformed every long-standing abuse in the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing military affairs, he swept away bureau abuses.

sentences.zh: 所奏覆多當上意，尚書倚之若左右手。

translations.literal: His memorial replies often pleased the emperor; the minister relied on him as on right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: His reports pleased the throne; the minister relied on him utterly.

sentences.zh: 汪直好邊功，以安南黎灝敗於老撾，欲乘間取之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi loved frontier glory; as the Annamese king Le Hao had been defeated by Laos, he wished to seize the chance to take the country.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, craving frontier glory, sought to conquer Annam after Le Hao's defeat by Laos.

sentences.zh: 言於帝，索永樂間討安南故牘。

translations.literal: He spoke to the emperor and demanded the Yongle-era files on the Annam campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor for Yongle files on the Annam war.

sentences.zh: 大夏匿弗予，密告尚書余子俊曰：「兵釁一開，西南立糜爛矣。」

translations.literal: Daxia hid them and did not give them, secretly telling Minister Yu Zijun: "Once the opening for war is made, the southwest will be ruined at once."
translations.idiomatic: Daxia hid the archives and secretly warned Minister Yu Zijun: "Once war begins, the southwest will be ruined overnight."

sentences.zh: 子俊悟，事得寢。

translations.literal: Zijun understood and the affair was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zijun understood and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮貢道故由鴉鶻關，至是請改由鴨綠江。

translations.literal: Korea's tribute route had gone through Yahu Pass; now they asked to change to the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: Korea sought to shift its tribute route from Yahu Pass to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 尚書將許之，大夏曰：「鴨綠道徑，祖宗朝豈不知，顧紆回數大鎮，此殆有微意。

translations.literal: The minister was about to agree; Daxia said: "The Yalu route is shorter. Did the ancestors not know that? Yet they chose the winding route through several great garrisons; there must be subtle intent in this.
translations.idiomatic: The minister was about to agree, but Daxia said: "The Yalu route is shorter. Did the founders not know that? Yet they deliberately wound the route through several major garrisons; there must have been a subtle reason.

sentences.zh: 不可許。」

translations.literal: It cannot be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: It must not be allowed."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The proposal was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The change was blocked.

sentences.zh: 中官阿九者，其兄任京衛經歷，以罪為大夏所笞。

translations.literal: The eunuch A Jiu's brother served as an experience officer in the capital guard and was flogged by Daxia for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch A Jiu's brother, a guard experience officer, was flogged by Daxia.

sentences.zh: 憲宗入其譖，捕系詔獄，令東廠偵之無所得。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor believed the slander, seized Daxia for the imperial prison, and ordered the Eastern Depot to investigate but found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong jailed him on slander; the Eastern Depot found no crime.

sentences.zh: 會懷恩力救，乃杖二十而釋之。

translations.literal: When Huai En strongly intervened, he was beaten twenty strokes and released.
translations.idiomatic: Huai En saved him with twenty strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遷福建右參政，以政績聞。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was moved to Right Administration Commissioner of Fujian, noted for governance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he became Fujian Right Administration Commissioner with a fine record.

sentences.zh: 聞父訃，一宿即行。

translations.literal: Hearing of his father's death, he set out after one night's rest.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he left after only one night.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年服闋，遷廣東右布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended in the second year of Hongzhi he was moved to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning in Hongzhi 2 he became Guangdong Right Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 田州、泗城不靖，大夏往諭，遂順命。

translations.literal: Tianzhou and Sicheng were unsettled; Daxia went to instruct them and they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Tianzhou and Sicheng by personal mission.

sentences.zh: 後山賊起，承檄討之。

translations.literal: Later mountain bandits rose and he took orders to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 令獲賊必生致，驗實乃坐，得生者過半。

translations.literal: He ordered that captives must be brought alive and punished only after verification; more than half survived.
translations.idiomatic: He required living captives and verified guilt; over half were spared.

sentences.zh: 改左，移浙江。

translations.literal: Shifted to the left post, he moved to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted left, he transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 六年春，河決張秋，詔博選才臣往治。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the Yellow River burst at Zhangqiu; the court widely chose able men to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 6 the Yellow River broke at Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王恕等以大夏薦，擢右副都御史以行。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Shu and others recommended Daxia; he was promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu recommended him as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief for the work.

sentences.zh: 乃自黃陵岡浚賈魯河，復浚孫家渡、四府營上流，以分水勢。

translations.literal: He dredged the Jia Lu River from Huangling Ridge and reopened Sunjiadu and Sifuying upstream to divide the current.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Jia Lu River and reopened upstream channels to split the flood.

sentences.zh: 而築長堤，起胙城歷東明、長垣抵徐州，亙三百六十里。

translations.literal: He also built a long dike from Zuocheng through Dongming and Changyuan to Xuzhou, spanning 360 li.
translations.idiomatic: He built a 360-li dike from Zuocheng to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 水大治，更名張秋鎮曰「安平鎮」。

translations.literal: The waters were greatly regulated, and Zhangqiu town was renamed "Anping Town."
translations.idiomatic: The waters were brought under control, and Zhangqiu was renamed "Anping Town."

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘉之，賜璽書褒美，語詳《河渠志》。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised him, granted a sealed edict of commendation—the story is in the Water Control Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong praised him in a sealed edict, detailed in the Water Control Treatises.

sentences.zh: 召為左副都御史，歷戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and rose to Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, then Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年命兼左僉都御史，往理宣府兵餉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered additionally as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief to manage Xuanfu army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was sent to manage Xuanfu army grain.

sentences.zh: 尚書周經謂曰：「塞上勢家子以市糴為私利，公毋以剛賈禍。」

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jing told him: "The sons of powerful frontier families use market grain purchases for private profit; do not bring disaster on yourself through severity."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jing warned him, "Powerful frontier families profit privately from grain markets; do not invite disaster by being too rigid."

sentences.zh: 大夏曰：「處天下事，以理不以勢，俟至彼圖之。」

translations.literal: Daxia said: 'Handle the world's affairs by principle, not by power; wait until I arrive to plan.'
translations.idiomatic: Daxia replied: 'I serve principle, not influence—we shall see on arrival.'

sentences.zh: 初，塞上糴買必粟千石、芻萬束乃得告納，以故，中官、武臣家得操利權。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier purchase required a thousand shi of grain and ten thousand bundles of fodder before delivery was accepted, so eunuch and military families held the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly only bulk lots of 1,000 shi and 10,000 fodder bundles were accepted, favoring the powerful.

sentences.zh: 大夏令有芻粟者，自百束十石以上皆許，勢家欲牟利無所得。

translations.literal: Daxia allowed anyone with fodder or grain from one hundred bundles or ten shi upward; the powerful could gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted lots as small as ten shi or one hundred bundles, ending their monopoly.

sentences.zh: 不兩月儲積棄羨，邊人蒙其利。

translations.literal: Within two months stores overflowed and frontier people reaped the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In two months stores overflowed and soldiers benefited.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，三疏移疾歸，築草堂東山下，讀書其中。

translations.literal: The next autumn he thrice memorialized illness and returned, building a thatched hall on East Mountain to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn he retired thrice and built a study on East Mountain.

sentences.zh: 越二年，廷臣交薦，起右都御史，總制兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Two years later the court repeatedly recommended him; he was raised Right Censor-in-Chief, overall commander of Liang-Guang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on he was made Right Censor-in-Chief, commander of Liang-Guang.

sentences.zh: 敕使及門，攜二僮行。

translations.literal: When the imperial messenger reached his door he set out with two servants.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled with only two servants when the edict arrived.

sentences.zh: 廣人故思大夏，鼓舞稱慶。

translations.literal: The people of Guang had long missed Daxia and cheered in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rejoiced at his return.

sentences.zh: 大夏為清吏治，捐供億，禁內外鎮守官私役軍士，盜賊為之衰止。

translations.literal: He cleaned administration, cut supplies, forbade frontier defenders from privately impressing soldiers, and banditry waned.
translations.idiomatic: He cleaned government, cut levies, barred private impressment, and bandits faded.

sentences.zh: 十五年拜兵部尚書，屢辭乃拜命。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was made Minister of War after several refusals.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became Minister of War after repeated refusals.

sentences.zh: 既召見，帝曰：「朕數用卿，數引疾何也？」

translations.literal: On audience the emperor said: "I have used you many times; why do you so often plead illness?"
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to audience, the emperor said, "I have called on you repeatedly; why do you repeatedly claim illness?"

sentences.zh: 大夏頓首言：「臣老且病，竊見天下民窮財盡，脫有不虞，責在兵部，自度力不辦，故辭耳。」

translations.literal: Daxia kowtowed and said: "Your servant is old and ill, and I privately see that the people under Heaven are poor and the treasury exhausted; if something unexpected occurs, the responsibility will lie with the Ministry of War, and judging myself unable to manage it, I therefore decline."
translations.idiomatic: Daxia kowtowed and said, "I am old and ill. I see that the people are exhausted and the treasury is empty; if anything unexpected happens, the blame will fall on the Ministry of War. I know I do not have the strength to manage it, and so I decline."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 南京、鳳陽大風拔木，河南、湖廣大水，京師苦雨沈陰。

translations.literal: Great wind in Nanjing and Fengyang uprooted trees; Henan and Huguang suffered floods; the capital endured oppressive rain.
translations.idiomatic: Storms, floods, and endless rain afflicted the realm.

sentences.zh: 大夏請凡事非祖宗舊而害軍民者，悉條上厘革。

translations.literal: Daxia asked that whatever harmed soldiers and people and was not ancestral practice be listed for reform.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to list all non-ancestral abuses harming soldiers and people.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月又言之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he spoke again.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 17 he spoke again.

sentences.zh: 帝命事當興革者，所司具實以聞，乃會廷臣條上十六事，皆權幸所不便者，相與力尼之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered offices to report facts on what should be reformed; the court then listed sixteen items, all inconvenient to the powerful, who together blocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen reforms were proposed, all opposed by favorites.

sentences.zh: 帝不能決，下再議。

translations.literal: The emperor could not decide and ordered further debate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated and ordered more debate.

sentences.zh: 大夏等言：「事屬外廷，悉蒙允行。

translations.literal: Daxia and the others said: "Matters belonging to the outer court were all graciously approved.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia and the others said, "All matters belonging to the outer court have been approved.

sentences.zh: 稍涉權貴，復令察核。

translations.literal: Those touching the powerful were sent back for review.
translations.idiomatic: Anything touching favorites was sent back for review.

sentences.zh: 臣等至愚，莫知所以。」

translations.literal: Your servants are utterly foolish and do not know the reason."
translations.idiomatic: We are too foolish to understand why."

sentences.zh: 久之，乃得旨：「傳奉官疏名以請；

translations.literal: After a long while, an imperial instruction was received: "For transmitted-order officials, submit memorials listing their names;
translations.idiomatic: After a long delay, an imperial order came down: "For honorary attendants appointed by transmitted command, submit their names by memorial;

sentences.zh: 幼匠、廚役減月米三斗；

translations.literal: apprentice artisans and kitchen laborers to lose three dou monthly grain;
translations.idiomatic: apprentices and kitchen staff lose three dou monthly;

sentences.zh: 增設中官，司禮監核奏；

translations.literal: new eunuch posts to be vetted by the Directorate of Ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: new eunuch posts need Ceremonies approval;

sentences.zh: 四衛勇士，禦馬監具數以聞。

translations.literal: the four guards' warriors—the Imperial Stud to report numbers.
translations.idiomatic: the four guards' warriors need Stud headcounts.

sentences.zh: 余悉如議。」

translations.literal: all the rest shall be as discussed."
translations.idiomatic: all the rest shall be as proposed."

sentences.zh: 織造、齋醮皆停罷，光祿省浮費巨萬計，而勇士虛冒之弊亦大減。

translations.literal: Weaving, vegetarian feasts, and other items were halted; the Court of Imperial Entertainments saved millions, and the abuse of false warriors was greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving and feasts stopped; Entertainments saved millions and false warriors were culled.

sentences.zh: 制下，舉朝歡悅。

translations.literal: When the orders issued the whole court rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejoiced when the edicts came down.

sentences.zh: 先是，外戚、近幸多幹恩澤，帝深知其害政，奮然欲振之。

translations.literal: Earlier, consort kin and favorites had often sought favors; the emperor knew they harmed government and was eager to reform.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew kin and favorites harmed rule and wished to reform.

sentences.zh: 因時多災異，復宣諭群臣，令各陳缺失。

translations.literal: With many disasters and omens he again told the ministers each to state what was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: After disasters he ordered ministers to list failings.

sentences.zh: 大夏乃復上數事。

translations.literal: Daxia again submitted several matters.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia submitted more reforms.

sentences.zh: 其年六月再陳兵政十害，且乞歸。

translations.literal: That sixth month he again set forth ten abuses of military policy and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he listed ten military abuses and begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，令弊端宜革者更祥具以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor refused and ordered abuses fit for reform to be detailed further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and demanded fuller detail on abuses.

sentences.zh: 於是，大夏舉南北軍轉漕番上之苦，及邊軍困敝、邊將侵克之狀極言之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daxia laid out the suffering of north-south troops in transport and canal labor and the frontier troops' exhaustion and generals' extortion in the strongest terms.
translations.idiomatic: He detailed transport misery, frontier exhaustion, and generals' graft.

sentences.zh: 帝乃召見大夏於便殿，問曰：「卿前言天下民窮財盡。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Daxia to the informal hall and asked: "You previously said that the people under Heaven are poor and the treasury exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Daxia to the informal hall and asked, "You said before that the people are poor and the treasury exhausted.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來征斂有常，何今日至此？」

translations.literal: Since the ancestors, levies have had fixed rules; why has it come to this today?"
translations.idiomatic: Since the founders, levies have followed fixed rules. Why have things come to this today?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「正謂不盡有常耳。

translations.literal: He answered: 'I mean they are not entirely fixed.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: 'Because they are no longer truly fixed.

sentences.zh: 如廣西歲取鐸木，廣東取香藥，費固以萬計，他可知矣。」

translations.literal: Guangxi yearly takes ironwood, Guangdong takes aromatics—costs already run to tens of thousands; the rest can be imagined.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi's ironwood and Guangdong's aromatics alone cost tens of thousands—imagine the rest.'

sentences.zh: 又問軍，對曰：「窮與民等。」

translations.literal: Asked about the army, he answered: 'They are as poor as the people.'
translations.idiomatic: On the army he said: 'Soldiers are as poor as civilians.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「居有月糧，出有行糧，何故窮？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'They have monthly rations in garrison and travel grain on campaign—why poor?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: 'They have monthly pay and campaign grain—why poor?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「其帥侵克過半，安得不窮。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Their commanders extort more than half; how could they not be poor?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Their commanders skim more than half; how could they not be poor?"

sentences.zh: 帝太息曰：「朕臨禦久，乃不知天下軍民困，何以為人主！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply: 'I have ruled long yet did not know soldiers and people suffer—how can I be lord of men!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: 'I never knew such suffering—what kind of ruler am I?'

sentences.zh: 遂下詔嚴禁。

translations.literal: An edict was issued strictly forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝方銳意太平，而劉健為首輔，馬文升以師臣長六卿，一時正人充布列位。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was keen on peace; Liu Jian was chief grand secretary and Ma Wensheng as tutor headed the six ministries; upright men filled the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong sought peace; Liu Jian led the cabinet and Ma Wensheng the ministries, with upright men throughout.

sentences.zh: 帝察知大夏方嚴，且練事，尤親信。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Daxia was strict and experienced in affairs and especially trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He found Daxia stern and seasoned and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 數召見決事，大夏亦隨事納忠。

translations.literal: He often summoned him to decide affairs, and Daxia offered loyal counsel on each.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned often, Daxia gave loyal counsel on every issue.

sentences.zh: 大同小警，帝用中官苗逵言，將出師。

translations.literal: A small alarm at Datong; on the eunuch Miao Kui's word the emperor wished to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: A Datong scare led the emperor, on eunuch Miao Kui's advice, to consider a campaign.

sentences.zh: 內閣劉健等力諫，帝猶疑之，召問大夏曰：「卿在廣，知苗逵延綏搗巢功乎？」

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others remonstrated strongly; the emperor still hesitated and summoned Daxia to ask: "When you were in Guang, did you know of Miao Kui's merit in raiding the nests at Yan and Sui?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and the others remonstrated forcefully, but the emperor still hesitated and asked Daxia, "When you were in the Guang region, did you know of Miao Kui's achievement in raiding the nests at Yan and Sui?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣聞之，所俘婦稚十數耳。

translations.literal: He answered: "Your servant heard of it; those captured were only a dozen-odd women and children.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia answered, "I heard of it. Those captured were only a dozen or so women and children.

sentences.zh: 賴朝廷威德，全師以歸。

translations.literal: Thanks to court majesty and virtue the whole army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned intact only by court prestige.

sentences.zh: 不然，未可知也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, it cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, we do not know what would have happened."

sentences.zh: 帝默然良久，問曰：「太宗頻出塞，今何不可？」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent for a long while and asked: "Taizong often went beyond the passes; why can this not be done now?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor asked, "Taizong often campaigned beyond the passes. Why can that not be done now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下神武固不後太宗，而將領士馬遠不逮。

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess is certainly not behind Taizong's, but the generals, officers, and horses fall far short.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia answered, "Your Majesty's martial spirit is certainly not inferior to Taizong's, but today's generals, officers, and horses fall far short.

sentences.zh: 且淇國公小違節制，舉數十萬眾委沙漠，奈何易言之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Duke of Qi once slighted discipline and left hundreds of thousands in the desert—how can it be spoken of lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Remember the Duke of Qi who lost an army in the desert—do not take this lightly.

sentences.zh: 度今上策惟守耳。」

translations.literal: Judging the present, the best policy is only defense."
translations.idiomatic: In present conditions, I judge that the best policy is defense alone."

sentences.zh: 都御史戴珊亦從旁贊決，帝遽曰：「微卿曹，朕幾誤。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan also supported the decision from the side; the emperor suddenly said: "Without you gentlemen, I nearly erred."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan also urged agreement from the side, and the emperor abruptly said, "Without you gentlemen, I would nearly have made a mistake."

sentences.zh: 由是，師不果出。

translations.literal: Thus the army did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition was canceled.

sentences.zh: 莊浪土帥魯麟為甘肅副將，求大將不得，恃其部眾強，徑歸莊浪。

translations.literal: Lu Lin, native chieftain of Zhuanglang, was Gansu vice general; denied a full command, he relied on his strong following and went straight back to Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lin of Zhuanglang, denied a major command, marched home with his troops.

sentences.zh: 廷臣懼生變，欲授以大帥印，又欲召還京，處之散地。

translations.literal: Court ministers feared trouble and wished either to give him the grand marshal's seal or summon him to the capital to a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers feared revolt and debated promoting or summoning him.

sentences.zh: 大夏請獎其先世忠順，而聽麟就閑。

translations.literal: Daxia asked to reward his family's past loyalty and let Lin live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia proposed honoring his ancestors and letting Lin retire.

sentences.zh: 麟素貪虐失眾心，兵柄已去無能為，竟怏怏病死。

translations.literal: Lin had long been greedy and cruel and lost popular support; without military power he could do nothing and died discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, unpopular and stripped of troops, died resentful.

sentences.zh: 帝欲宿兵近地為左右輔。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to station troops nearby as left and right supports.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted nearby garrisons as flanks.

sentences.zh: 大夏言：「保定設都司統五衛，祖宗意當亦如此。

translations.literal: Daxia said: "Baoding has a regional military commission overseeing five guards; the ancestors' intent must also have been like this.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia said, "Baoding has a regional command overseeing five guards; the founders must have intended the same arrangement here.

sentences.zh: 請遣還操軍萬人為西衛，納京東兵密雲、薊州為東衛。」

translations.literal: Please send back ten thousand drill troops to make the western guard, and take the Jingdong troops at Miyun and Jizhou to make the eastern guard."
translations.idiomatic: Send back ten thousand drill troops to form the western guard, and assign the Jingdong troops at Miyun and Jizhou to form the eastern guard."

sentences.zh: 帝報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 中官監京營者恚失兵，揭飛語宮門。

translations.literal: Eunuchs supervising the capital camps, angry at losing troops, posted slander at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Camp eunuchs, losing troops, posted libel at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 帝以示大夏曰：「宮門豈外人能至？

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Daxia and said: "How could outsiders reach the palace gate?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed it to Daxia and said, "How could outsiders reach the palace gate?

sentences.zh: 必此曹不利失兵耳。」

translations.literal: It must be these men, who are harmed by losing troops."
translations.idiomatic: It must be these fellows, angry at losing troops."

sentences.zh: 由是，間不得行。

translations.literal: Thus the plan could not be carried out for a time.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was stalled.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭大夏曰：「臨事輒思召卿，慮越職而止。

translations.literal: The emperor once told Daxia: "Whenever affairs arise, I think of summoning you, but fearing that I would overstep your office, I stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Daxia, "Whenever affairs arise, I think of summoning you, but I stop because I fear overstepping the bounds of your office.

sentences.zh: 後有當行罷者，具揭帖以進。」

translations.literal: Hereafter, when there is something that should be carried out or stopped, submit it fully in a sealed note."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, when something should be done or halted, submit it in a sealed note."

sentences.zh: 大夏頓首曰：「事之可否，外付府部，內咨閣臣可矣。

translations.literal: Daxia kowtowed and said: "For whether affairs may or may not be done, it is enough to entrust them externally to the offices and ministries, and internally to consult the Grand Secretariat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia kowtowed and said, "Whether a policy should be carried out can be handled by the offices and ministries outside and by consultation with the Grand Secretariat inside.

sentences.zh: 揭帖滋弊，不可為後世法。」

translations.literal: Sealed notes breed abuses and must not become a model for later ages."
translations.idiomatic: Sealed notes breed abuse and must not become a precedent for later generations."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the answer.

sentences.zh: 又嘗問：「天下何時太平？」

translations.literal: He also once asked: "When will the realm be at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once also asked, "When will the realm be at peace?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「求治亦難太急。

translations.literal: He answered: "In seeking order, it is also difficult to be too hasty.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia answered, "In seeking good order, one must not be too impatient.

sentences.zh: 但用人行政悉與大臣面議，當而後行，久之天下自治。」

translations.literal: Only discuss appointments and policy face to face with the great ministers, act after they are appropriate, and after a long time the realm will govern itself."
translations.idiomatic: Discuss appointments and policies face to face with the ministers, act only when the measures are right, and in time the realm will settle itself."

sentences.zh: 嘗乘間言四方鎮守中官之害。

translations.literal: He once seized a chance to speak of the harm of frontier eunuch defenders.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of the harm of frontier eunuch defenders.

sentences.zh: 帝問狀，對曰：「臣在兩廣見諸文武大吏供億不能敵一鎮守，其煩費可知。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the situation, and he answered: "When your servant was in the two Guangs, I saw that the supplies for all the civil and military great officials could not match those for one defending eunuch; from this the burdensome expense can be known."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about the situation, and Daxia answered, "When I was in the two Guang, I saw that all the civil and military grandees together did not consume as much support as a single defending eunuch. From that you can know the expense."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然祖宗來設此久，安能遽革？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yet the ancestors have established these posts for a long time; how can they be suddenly abolished?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But the ancestors established these posts long ago. How can they be abolished suddenly?

sentences.zh: 第自今必廉如鄧原、麥秀者而後用，不然則已之。」

translations.literal: Only from now on, use men only after they are honest like Deng Yuan and Mai Xiu; otherwise stop it."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, appoint only men as honest as Deng Yuan and Mai Xiu; otherwise, do not appoint them."

sentences.zh: 大夏頓首稱善。

translations.literal: Daxia kowtowed in approval.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia kowtowed in approval.

sentences.zh: 大夏每被召，跪禦榻前。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned Daxia knelt before the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia knelt before the couch when summoned.

sentences.zh: 帝左右顧，近侍輒引避。

translations.literal: The emperor glanced about and attendants at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants withdrew when the emperor glanced aside.

sentences.zh: 嘗對久，憊不能興，呼司禮太監李榮掖之出。

translations.literal: Once after long discussion he was too weary to rise; the Director of Ceremonies Li Rong was called to help him out.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Rong helped the exhausted Daxia from the hall.

sentences.zh: 一日早朝，大夏固在班，帝偶未見，明日諭曰：「卿昨失朝耶？

translations.literal: One day at morning court, Daxia was actually in the ranks, but the emperor happened not to see him; the next day he instructed him, saying: "Did you miss court yesterday?
translations.idiomatic: One morning Daxia was in the court ranks, but the emperor happened not to see him. The next day the emperor said, "Were you absent from court yesterday?

sentences.zh: 恐御史糾，不果召卿。」

translations.literal: I feared the censors would impeach you, and therefore did not summon you."
translations.idiomatic: I feared the censors would impeach you, so I held back from summoning you."

sentences.zh: 其受眷深如此。

translations.literal: Such was the depth of his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 特賜玉帶、麒麟服，所賚金幣、上尊，歲時不絕。

translations.literal: He was specially granted a jade belt and python robe; gifts of gold, coins, and fine wine never ceased through the year.
translations.idiomatic: He received jade belt, python robe, and endless gifts.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孝宗崩，武宗嗣位，承詔請撤四方鎮守中官非額設者。

translations.literal: Before long Xiaozong died and Wuzong succeeded; carrying out the edict he asked to withdraw non-statutory frontier eunuch defenders.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzong's accession he moved to withdraw extra frontier eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 帝止撤均州齊元。

translations.literal: The emperor only withdrew Qi Yuan at Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qi Yuan at Junzhou was removed.

sentences.zh: 大夏復議上應撤者二十四人，又奏減皇城、京城守視中官，皆不納。

translations.literal: Daxia again listed twenty-four who should be withdrawn and memorialized to reduce inner-palace and capital guard eunuchs—all rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He listed twenty-four more for withdrawal and cuts to palace guards—all rejected.

sentences.zh: 頃之，列上傳奉武臣當汰者六百八十三人，報可。

translations.literal: Soon he listed six hundred eighty-three honorary military men to be dismissed and was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred eighty-three honorary soldiers were approved for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 大漢將軍薛福敬等四十八人亦當奪官，福敬等故不入侍以激帝怒。

translations.literal: Forty-eight Great Han generals including Xue Fujing should also lose rank; Fujing and others had deliberately stayed from attendance to provoke the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight Great Han generals including Xue Fujing were to be struck; they had boycotted court to anger the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝遽命復之，而責兵部對狀，欲加罪。

translations.literal: The emperor at once ordered them restored and blamed the Ministry of War for a hearing, intending punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored them and threatened to punish the war ministry.

sentences.zh: 中官寧瑾頓首曰：「此先帝遺命，陛下列之登極詔書，不宜罪。」

translations.literal: The eunuch Ning Jin kowtowed and said: "This is the late emperor's testamentary command; Your Majesty listed it in the accession edict, and it should not be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ning Jin kowtowed and said, "This was the late emperor's dying command, and Your Majesty included it in the accession edict. It should not be punished."

sentences.zh: 帝意乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 中官韋興者，成化末得罪久廢，至是夤緣守均州。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wei Xing, punished at the end of Chenghua and long idle, now curried favor to defend Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Disgraced eunuch Wei Xing sought to defend Junzhou by favor.

sentences.zh: 言官交諫，大夏等再三爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Remonstrators protested in concert; Daxia and others argued again and again—all unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators and Daxia protested repeatedly in vain.

sentences.zh: 正德元年春，又言：「鎮守中官，如江西董讓、薊州劉瑯、陜西劉雲、山東朱雲貪殘尤甚，乞按治。」

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Zhengde, he again said: "Among defending eunuchs, Dong Rang of Jiangxi, Liu Lang of Jizhou, Liu Yun of Shaanxi, and Zhu Yun of Shandong are especially greedy and cruel; I beg that they be investigated and punished."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Zhengde 1 he again said, "Among the defending eunuchs, Dong Rang in Jiangxi, Liu Lang in Jizhou, Liu Yun in Shaanxi, and Zhu Yun in Shandong are especially rapacious and cruel. I ask that they be investigated and punished."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 大夏自知言不見用，數上章乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Daxia knew his words were useless and repeatedly asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was ignored, Daxia begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，詔加太子太保，賜敕馳驛歸，給廩隸如制。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a farewell decree and relay transport home, with stipends as regulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was made Junior Guardian and sent home with full honors.

sentences.zh: 給事中王翊、張襘請留之，吏部亦請如翊、襘言，不報。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Wang Yi and Zhang Gui asked to keep him; Personnel also asked as Yi and Gui said—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi and Zhang Gui and Personnel asked to retain him—no answer.

sentences.zh: 大夏忠誠懇篤，遇知孝宗，忘身徇國，於權幸多所裁抑。

translations.literal: Daxia was loyal and earnest; meeting Xiaozong's trust he forgot himself for the state and curbed the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal to Xiaozong, he served the state and curbed favorites.

sentences.zh: 嘗請嚴核勇士，為劉瑾所惡。

translations.literal: He once asked to strictly review warriors and was hated by Liu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His strict review of warriors angered Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉宇亦憾大夏，遂與焦芳譖於瑾曰：「籍大夏家，可當邊費十二。」

translations.literal: Liu Yu also resented Daxia, and with Jiao Fang slandered him to Jin, saying: "Confiscating Daxia's household could cover twelve years of frontier expenses."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu also resented Daxia, and he and Jiao Fang slandered him to Jin, saying, "If Daxia's estate is confiscated, it can cover twelve years of frontier expenses."

sentences.zh: 三年九月，假田州岑猛事，逮系詔獄。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, using the Tianzhou chief Cen Meng affair as pretext, he was seized for the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 3 he was jailed on the Cen Meng pretext.

sentences.zh: 瑾欲坐以激變律死，都御史屠滽持不可，瑾謾罵曰：「即不死，可無戍耶？」

translations.literal: Jin wished to sentence him to death under the statute on inciting disorder; Censor-in-Chief Tu Yong firmly objected, and Jin cursed: "Even if he does not die, can there be no garrison exile?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin wanted to execute him under the statute on inciting disorder, but Censor-in-Chief Tu Yong blocked it; Jin cursed, "Even if he does not die, can he not at least be sent to garrison exile?"

sentences.zh: 李東陽為婉解，且瑾诇大夏家實貧，乃坐戍極邊。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang mediated gently, and when Jin spied and found Daxia's house truly poor, he was sentenced to the farthest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang mediated; finding Daxia poor, Jin exiled him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初擬廣西，芳曰：「是送若歸也」，遂改肅州。

translations.literal: At first Guangxi was proposed, but Fang said, "That is sending you home," and so it was changed to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi was first proposed, but Fang said, "That is sending him home," so the destination was changed to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 大夏年已七十三，布衣徒步過大明門下，叩首而去。

translations.literal: Daxia was already seventy-three; in plain clothes he walked past the Daming Gate, kowtowed below, and left.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-three he walked in plain clothes past the Daming Gate, kowtowed, and left.

sentences.zh: 觀者嘆息泣下，父老攜筐送食，所至為罷市、焚香祝劉尚書生還。

translations.literal: Viewers sighed and wept; elders brought baskets of food; wherever he passed markets closed and incense was burned praying the Minister Liu would return alive.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds wept; markets closed; incense burned for his safe return.

sentences.zh: 比至戍所，諸司憚瑾，絕饋問，儒學生徒傳食之。

translations.literal: At the garrison all offices feared Jin and cut off supplies; Confucian students alone brought him food.
translations.idiomatic: Officials feared Jin and cut supplies; only students fed him.

sentences.zh: 遇團操，輒荷戈就伍。

translations.literal: When regimental drill was held he took up a spear and joined the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At drill he took a spear and joined ranks.

sentences.zh: 所司固辭，大夏曰：「軍，固當役也。」

translations.literal: The responsible office firmly declined, but Daxia said: "A soldier certainly ought to serve."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office firmly refused, but Daxia insisted, "A soldier should serve."

sentences.zh: 所攜止一仆。

translations.literal: He brought only one servant.
translations.idiomatic: He had only one servant.

sentences.zh: 或問何不挈子姓，曰：「吾宦時，不為子孫乞恩澤。

translations.literal: When someone asked why he did not take his sons and grandsons, he said: "When I was in office, I did not beg favor for my descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why he did not bring his sons and grandsons, he said, "When I was in office, I never sought favors for my descendants.

sentences.zh: 今垂老得罪，忍令同死戍所耶？」

translations.literal: Now that I am old and guilty, how could I bear to make them die with me at the garrison place?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, old and convicted, how could I bear to make them die with me at the garrison?"

sentences.zh: 大夏既遣戍，瑾猶摭他事罰米輸塞上者再。

translations.literal: After Daxia was exiled Jin still seized other matters and twice fined him grain for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jin twice fined him grain for the border after exile.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，赦歸。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year amnesty brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty in summer of year 5 brought him home.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored and retired.

sentences.zh: 清軍御史王相請復廩隸，錄其子孫。

translations.literal: Purging-army censor Wang Xiang asked to restore stipends and enroll his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang sought stipends and offices for his family.

sentences.zh: 中官用事者終嗛之，不許。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in power still resented him and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful eunuchs refused.

sentences.zh: 大夏歸，教子孫力田謀食。

translations.literal: Daxia returned and taught his sons and grandsons to farm for food.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his family to farm.

sentences.zh: 稍贏，散之故舊宗族。

translations.literal: When there was a surplus he gave it to old friends and clan.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus went to friends and clan.

sentences.zh: 預自為壙誌，曰：「無使人飾美，俾懷愧地下也。」

translations.literal: He prepared his own tomb inscription beforehand, saying: "Do not let people embellish my virtues and cause me to feel shame underground."
translations.idiomatic: He prepared his own tomb inscription in advance, saying, "Do not let people adorn me with false praise and leave me ashamed underground."

sentences.zh: 十一年五月卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year he died at eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of year 11, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚忠宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously Grand Preceptor Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 大夏嘗言：「居官以正己為先。

translations.literal: Daxia once said: "In holding office, correcting oneself comes first.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia once said, "In office, the first priority is to correct oneself.

sentences.zh: 不獨當戒利，亦當遠名。」

translations.literal: One should not only guard against profit, but also keep far from fame."
translations.idiomatic: One must not only guard against profit, but also keep away from reputation."

sentences.zh: 又言：「人生蓋棺論定，一日未死，即一日憂責未已。」

translations.literal: He also said: "A man's life is judged when the coffin is closed; for each day he is not yet dead, his worries and responsibilities are not yet finished."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A person is judged only when the coffin is closed. So long as one day of life remains, one day of care and responsibility remains."

sentences.zh: 其被逮也，方鋤菜園中，入室攜數百錢，跨小驢就道。

translations.literal: When arrested he was hoeing the vegetable garden; entering the house he took a few hundred coins, mounted a small donkey, and took the road.
translations.idiomatic: Arrested while hoeing, he took a few coins and a donkey to prison.

sentences.zh: 赦歸，有門下生為巡撫者，枉百里謁之。

translations.literal: After amnesty a former student who was grand coordinator traveled a hundred li to visit.
translations.idiomatic: A former student, now grand coordinator, traveled far to visit.

sentences.zh: 道遇扶犁者，問孰為尚書家，引之登堂，即大夏也。

translations.literal: On the road he met a man plowing and asked which was the minister's house; the man led him to the hall—it was Daxia himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he asked a plowman for the minister's house—it was Daxia.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮使者在鴻臚寺館遇大夏邑子張生，因問起居曰：「吾國聞劉東山名久矣。」

translations.literal: A Korean envoy staying at the Court of State Ceremonial hostel met Zhang, a townsman of Daxia, and through him asked after Daxia's health, saying: "Our country has long heard the name of Liu of East Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: A Korean envoy at the Court of State Ceremonial hostel met Daxia's townsman Zhang and sent greetings through him, saying, "Our country has long known the name of Liu of East Mountain."

sentences.zh: 安南使者入貢曰：「聞劉尚書戍邊，今安否？」

translations.literal: An Annamese tribute envoy entering court said: 'We heard Minister Liu was exiled to the frontier—is he now well?'
translations.idiomatic: An Annamese envoy asked: 'We heard Minister Liu was banished—is he safe?'

sentences.zh: 其為外國所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which foreign states held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his renown abroad.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王恕砥礪風節，馬文升練達政體，劉大夏篤棐自將，皆具經國之遠猷，蘊畜君之正誌。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Wang Shu honed his integrity, Ma Wensheng was practiced in government forms, and Liu Daxia was steadfast in self-restraint—all possessed far-reaching plans for governing the state and harbored the ruler's upright purpose.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Shu tempered his integrity, Wensheng mastered statecraft, and Daxia held himself with discipline—each bore far-reaching statecraft and upright loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 綢繆庶務，數進讜言，跡其居心行己，磊落光明，剛方鯁亮，有古大臣節概。

translations.literal: They managed myriad affairs, repeatedly offered loyal counsel; tracing their hearts and conduct, they were open and bright, firm and upright, with the bearing of great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: They managed affairs, spoke frankly, and in heart and deed were luminous, firm, and worthy of ancient great ministers.

sentences.zh: 歷事累朝，享有眉壽，朝野屬望，名重遠方。

translations.literal: Serving many reigns, they enjoyed long life; court and country looked to them, and their fame weighed heavily in distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: Serving many reigns into great age, they were pillars at court and famed abroad.

sentences.zh: 《詩》頌老成，《書》稱黃髮，三臣者近之矣。

translations.literal: The Odes praise seasoned elders, the Documents honor white-haired worthies—these three ministers approached that ideal.
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes honor elders and the Documents honor white-haired sages, these three approached that ideal.

sentences.zh: 恕昧遠名之戒，以作傳見疏。

translations.literal: Shu ignored the warning against seeking distant fame and was estranged for having a biography written.
translations.idiomatic: Shu forgot the warning against vainglory and was estranged for his published biography.

sentences.zh: 而文升，大夏被遇孝宗之朝，明良相契，荃宰一心。

translations.literal: Wensheng and Daxia met their fortune in the Xiaozong reign, ruler and minister in harmony, sharing one will to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng and Daxia flourished under Xiaozong, ruler and ministers of one mind.

sentences.zh: 迨至宦豎乘權，耆舊擯斥，進退之際所系詎不重哉！

translations.literal: When palace eunuchs seized power and the aged were cast out, how weighty were the stakes at their coming and going!
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs ruled and elders were driven out, how momentous their rise and fall proved!
